stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'BJP district president misbehaved with woman BLO':Husband's mobile phone snatched; planning to cut PDA votes in Amethi
stories.summary: A case of misbehavior with a BLO during SIR has emerged against the BJP district president in Amethi. According to the woman's husband, BJP supporters assaulted them. They were humiliated. Their mobile phone was snatched. A video of the incident has also surfaced, showing arguments between both parties. The BLO's husband has complained about the matter to the SDM. The incident occurred in the Sangrampur police station area. SDM Ashish Singh says that the matter is being investigated. Meanwhile, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has tweeted on 'X' demanding strict action against the culprits from the state government and administration. Akhilesh wrote - This is a very serious matter that the Amethi BJP district president assaulted a BLO. They pressured the female BLO to get PDA society's votes cancelled and increase votes for BJP supporters. When she didn't work according to their wishes, the female BLO was humiliated. The incident took place on Wednesday afternoon in Thengha village of Sangrampur development block. Here, BLO Subhadra Maurya was going door-to-door conducting voter verification work. According to the woman, some BJP people arrived at the scene. They started protesting. They pressured to remove some people's votes. Then they started misbehaving. They began beating her husband, Rakesh Kumar Maurya. Even papers were snatched. The mobile phone was taken away when trying to record a video. A video of the incident has also emerged, which shows an argument between some women and men. BLO said - They grabbed husband's collar, beat him up BLO Subhadra Maurya said - she had reached the spot with her husband. During this time, her husband said that instead of setting up the booth in the village, it should be set up in the school premises. Any meeting should be held at the school booth only. Why is it being organized in the village? Someone went and told this to the concerned people. After this, about 5 youths from the BJP reached the spot. They grabbed her husband's collar. During the intervention, there was fighting, pushing, and shoving. The BJP district president was present at some distance. The youths had reached there on his signal. They snatched my mobile and got physical BLO's husband, Rakesh Maurya, said that if the BJP district president wanted, this incident could have been prevented. The accused are residents of the same village and are known from before. The youths snatched his mobile phone and got physical with him. After my mobile was snatched, that young man went to the BJP district president. I have served as the district secretary of Congress. I have also worked in other positions. I have submitted a complaint letter to SDM Ashish Singh demanding action. BJP District President says - This is a conspiracy to defame BJP District President Sudhanshu Shukla says that Congress is continuously strangling democratic values. We are being defamed by making such fabricated allegations. My name is being dragged unnecessarily. No such incident happened at the spot. The BLO is being negligent in their work. I was not even present at the spot.

stories.title: Chinese kite string cuts biker’s throat in Lucknow:Rushed to trauma centre, dies after heavy blood loss despite emergency treatment
stories.summary: MR died due to a Chinese kite string cutting his neck in Lucknow. He was riding a bike when the Chinese kite string got caught around his neck. Covered in blood, he fell off his bike and struggled for about 10 minutes. Passersby took him to the trauma center, where he died during treatment. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Shoaib (33). The incident occurred on Wednesday afternoon, around 2 PM, at the Haiderganj overbridge in the Khala Bazar police station area. Brother-in-law Faiz said that at 3:30 in the afternoon, his wife called to inform him that Shoaib had met with an accident. Upon receiving the information, he rushed to the Trauma Center. His ECG was in progress there. Shortly after, Shoaib passed away. Shoaib was an MR at the Zydus company. His family includes wife Fouzia, daughters 7-year-old Bushra and 2-year-old Ikra. His sister is a doctor in Delhi. Chinese kite string cut neck artery Doctors treating Shoaib said - Shoaib was brought in critical condition. Treatment was started in the emergency department. His neck arteries were cut. He had lost a lot of blood. He could not be saved. He died due to the severing of neck arteries. Inspector Bazar Khala Brijesh Singh said - The incident happened at 2 PM. Police reached upon receiving information and took him to the hospital for treatment, where he died during treatment. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Further action will be taken based on the complaint. Chinese Manja is banned in UP The sale of Chinese manja is completely banned in UP. Despite this, it is still being sold. In India, kite string is made from normal thread, but in China, nylon is used along with metallic powder. Glass and iron powder are also mixed into it to make the edge sharper. Due to the nylon thread, tension increases when the screw fights andthe Chinese manja does not cut. This manja mixed with glass and iron powder is sufficient for cutting the throat. Chinese manja becomes deadly....

stories.title: Grand 10km procession of 55 luxury cars held in Jhansi:Number plate on Audi reads 'Rao Sahab'; creating buzz for Pradhan elections
stories.summary: A young man took out a procession of 55 cars in Jhansi on Wednesday. The convoy included expensive cars like Audi, Thar, Scorpio, Baleno and Innova. The cars had BJP and SP flags mounted on them. Many cars were fitted with hooters. The Audi leading the convoy had 'Rao Sahab' written on its number plate. The young man demonstrated his power in the village and kept playing DJ music at high volume. The police had no clue about this procession. The incident happened on Tuesday, and the video emerged today, on Wednesday. The father of the young man, showing his dominance to the villagers, had previously contested the Pradhan election. However, he was defeated then. The young man is now preparing to contest the election himself. Performed stunts hanging from vehicles Shishupal Yadav from Amarpur village and his father Veeran Pal Yadav are farmers. They own 4 acres of land. One acre of land was sold to the Bundelkhand Industrial Authority, for which they received compensation worth crores of rupees. Shishupal is preparing to contest the upcoming panchayat election for the position of pradhan. To strengthen his candidacy, Shishupal demonstrated his power in the village on Tuesday. In the morning, a DJ was set up on a mini pickup truck outside the village, where all luxury vehicles gathered. After this, Shishupal Yadav reached his supporters and proceeded through the village streets with his convoy while playing loud DJ music. Shishupal Yadav himself led the procession. He sat in a red Audi car. A youth kept making videos while hanging out of this car's sunroof. Meanwhile, youths in several other cars were seen hanging from windows and doors. The convoy went from one village to another in the gram panchayat. A show of strength was demonstrated by taking out a procession for about 10 kilometres. Hooters mounted on many vehicles in the procession kept blaring. Shared video himself, wrote - Future Pradhan The show of strength video was uploaded by Shishupal Yadav on his Instagram account on Wednesday, which reads "Future Pradhan". Shishupal Yadav's father, Viren Yadav, had tried his luck in the panchayat elections but lost. Now the son is preparing to contest the Pradhan election. Station In-charge Says - No Information about the Procession In this matter, when Dainik Bhaskar contacted the Raksa station in-charge, he said that he has no information about any such procession. Panchayat Elections will be held in UP between April-July Minister OP Rajbhar says - Ballot Papers have reached districts, voter list will come on february 28 Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar made a big claim regarding panchayat elections in UP on Tuesday. He said - UP government has completed preparations for conducting panchayat elections. Elections will be held on schedule. Rajbhar is the Panchayati Raj Minister in the Yogi government. He was in Varanasi on Tuesday. He put an end to speculations about panchayat elections being held along with the 2027 assembly elections. He said- Panchayat elections will be held before assembly elections. Ballot papers have been printed and reached all districts for this. District Election Officers have started their homework. Final publication of voter list on February 28 Rajbhar said - The final publication of the voter list will be on February 28, 2026. Prospective candidates have been advised to get their supporters' names added before the final list comes out. Panchayat elections will be conducted through ballot papers, not through EVMs. Elections will be held between April and July OP Rajbhar said - Panchayat elections will be held before the Assembly elections. However, he avoided announcing exact dates. He said - The entire process of Panchayat elections will be completed between April and July 2026. In the first phase, votes will be cast for Gram Pradhan, BDC (Block Panchayat Member) and District Panchayat members. This will be followed by indirect elections for Block Chief and District Panchayat President. The districts are ready for this, and ballot papers have been delivered to the districts. Their notification will be done soon.

stories.title: Father of sisters who died by suicide married twice:Had affair with sister-in-law; told daughters to stop using mobile phones
stories.summary: During initial questioning, the girls’ father, Chetan Kumar, told police that his daughters were addicted to Korean online games. However, after detailed questioning, police found that Chetan had suffered losses of nearly ₹2 crore in share trading, due to which the education of all three daughters had been stopped around three years ago. With no school to attend, the girls spent most of their time at home on mobile phones. Police said the family’s financial condition worsened further, and electricity at their rented flat was cut due to unpaid bills. Chetan later sold the girls’ mobile phones to manage expenses, leading to frequent arguments. The phones were bought back after he borrowed money from a friend. Police said disputes continued at home, and during one argument, Chetan allegedly threatened to get his daughters married, which may have caused further distress. Investigators believe a combination of financial stress, family tension, and isolation may have led the sisters to take the extreme step. An eyewitness, businessman Arun, told police that he saw one girl sitting on the railing. She was pulled back once, returned to the railing after a few seconds, was briefly hugged by someone, and then fell. Further investigation revealed that Chetan lost his job during COVID and later tried share trading and marketing work, both of which failed. He had been living in a rented flat in Ghaziabad for three years. Police also confirmed that Chetan had married twice, with his second marriage to his first wife’s younger sister. Two of the three girls were born from the second marriage. Police said the investigation is ongoing. Happiness came to the family when children were born After this, Hina had 2 daughters, bringing happiness to the home. Meanwhile, something amazing happened when the first wife also had a child during this time. But these occasions were also somewhat difficult for the family, because the job and share broking were not bringing in enough money to meet all the family's needs. Now fights started happening at home, Chetan's closeness with both wives' sisters (salis) also started increasing, leading to domestic conflicts. The sisters started saying that they were being tortured this way, their lives were ruined, and if he wanted to be with their sister, he should have married her instead. Due to losses in Chetan's business and these activities, his brothers also created distance in their relationships, which is why family members did not reach the postmortem house. After the triple suicide, different statements from Chetan have emerged, in which he says that his daughter had not been going to school for 2 years. He also told police officers that when schools closed during COVID, his daughters failed. After this, the daughters stopped going to school. The fact that all three girls were not attending school itself indicates their financial situation. Three days ago, Chetan had told both his elder daughters that they are not allowed to use mobile phones, saying, "I have already made you quit studies; my situation is not such that all these online games can be played, so I will get both of you married soon." Video after suicide, mother screaming The night video has also emerged, showing the bodies of all three girls lying on the ground. The girl's mother is cursing, indicating there may have been some conflict between Chetan's two wives. During conversations, it was also revealed that Chetan's youngest sister-in-law (wife's youngest sister) used to frequently visit. The youngest sister-in-law is unmarried. It was reported that she was also inside the house on the night of the incident. Neighbors are also shocked in this matter, as Chetan was not seen coming and going for 2 to 3 days. According to people living in the neighborhood, Chetan's wife was often seen drying clothes on the balcony. However, there wasn't much contact with anyone. Eyewitness Account of Triple Suicide I saw a girl sitting on the railing at night The girls were attempting suicide. It was around 2 o'clock at night. Arun was present in the flat directly opposite. He is a businessman by profession, and he was watching these girls at that time. At first, he thought it was a couple, but later he realized they were girls. Let's understand what Arun saw in his own words... He says - I saw that the light was on in the balcony of the opposite flat. When I looked there, someone was sitting on the railing at that time. This seemed very abnormal to me. From what I saw, it appeared to be a couple attempting suicide, but someone was pulling them back from behind. At that time, it didn't seem like they were girls. This way, she climbed down from the railing once. But after a few seconds, she came back up on the railing. Someone embraced her from behind, and now there were 3 shadows. Then I saw that the one at the back was trying to save her. But then they fell down one by one. They said - I called the ambulance that night itself. When the police arrived, I told them everything I had seen. The police are also investigating the angle whether the two elder sisters might have pushed the 12-year-old younger sister first and then committed suicide. 3 sisters jumped from the ninth floor of the building Three sisters committed suicide by jumping from the balcony of the ninth floor in Ghaziabad. According to police, at 2 AM on Tuesday night, they locked the room from inside, then placed a stool and jumped one by one from the balcony. They are approximately 12, 14, and 16 years old. According to their father, all three daughters were addicted to task-based Korean love games. They always stayed together. They would bathe together and go to the toilet together. They were so addicted to the game that they had quit school. Media reports claim that their father forbade them from playing games and scolded them. Because of this, they took this step. Police found a diary in the room where the three sisters slept. An 18-page suicide note was found written in it. Police claim the note states: "Mom-Dad sorry... I can't quit the game. Now you will realize how much we loved the game that you wanted us to quit." The incident occurred at flat number 907 of Bharat City B-1 tower. Additional Police Commissioner Law and Order Alok Priyadarshi said - Investigation so far has revealed that all three committed suicide. They used to play games on mobile. The circumstances under which the suicide was committed are being investigated. Clues will be found from suicide note and mobile Additional Police Commissioner Law and Order Alok Priyadarshi said - Investigation so far has revealed that 3 girls committed suicide. It also came to light that this is not related to gaming apps. The girls used to watch Korean movies. Chetan's financial condition was also not good. ACP Shalimar Garden Atul Kumar Singh says - The girls' father does online trading, has been living on rent in Bharat City Society for 3 years, and they are originally from Delhi. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, these girls have not attended school regularly. DCP Nimish Patil said - Investigation so far has revealed that all three girls died by suicide. We have also found a note, which is being officially investigated. No app name has come up in the investigation, but the note states that the girls were influenced by Korean culture. That's why they committed suicide. The girls' father had two marriages, and they have different mothers.

BJP tension rises after Swatantra Dev–Brijbhushan clash in UP A public confrontation over water scheme failures has triggered a Kurmi–Lodhi caste debate. MS Dhoni backs India’s chances in 2026 T20 World Cup Dhoni expressed confidence in the current Indian squad’s ability to handle pressure. stories.title: CM Nitish Kumar’s son takes e-rickshaw ride in Mathura:He strolls through lanes in slippers, without bodyguards or convoy
stories.summary: Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's son Nishant Kumar is visiting Mathura and Vrindavan. On Tuesday, he toured Vrindavan with his family in an e-rickshaw. They walked through the streets. First, Nishant Kumar went to Yamuna Ghat by e-rickshaw. He folded his hands and bowed to Mother Yamuna. After this, he reached the Banke Bihari temple and performed proper darshan-worship. During this time, his simplicity remained a topic of discussion among people. Nishant Kumar was accompanied by 4-5 people. They travelled in the e-rickshaw, paying just 10 rupees per passenger. There were no bodyguards with him, nor was any VIP protocol observed. Nishant Kumar's journey was completely private and spiritual. Wearing a kurta-pyjama and slippers, Nishant Kumar was seen roaming in the streets of Vrindavan, chanting 'Radhe-Radhe'. Visited ISKCON temple, had darshan at Banke Bihari Nishant Kumar was seen roaming in the streets of Vrindavan with his relatives on Wednesday afternoon. During his stay in Vrindavan, he visited and worshipped at major temples, including the ISKCON temple, the Banke Bihari temple and others. Nishant is the only son of Chief Minister Nitish Kumar and Manju Sinha. His mother, Manju Sinha, was once a school teacher, who passed away in 2007. Nishant Kumar received his early education from St. Karen's School in Patna. After this, he completed his further studies at Woodstock School (Manav Bharti India International School) in Mussoorie. Nishant Kumar studied Software Engineering from Birla Institute of Technology (BIT), Mesra, Ranchi and is an engineer by profession. Staying away from politics, he prefers to spend most of his time in personal and spiritual activities. He has not married yet. Nishant may enter politics after Holi, CM may leave chairman position After Holi, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's son Nishant Kumar may enter politics. Inside the Janata Dal United (JDU), preparations for this have begun. According to sources, the election for JDU's new national president is to be held in March. Currently, Nitish Kumar is handling the party's command. There is a discussion that he may leave the position of national president along with Nishant Kumar's entry. After the spectacular victory in the Bihar Assembly elections, preparations have begun to rebuild JDU from scratch. A membership drive is being conducted for organisational expansion. The target is to connect one crore new people to the party. After this, elections will be held for important party positions from the panchayat to the National level. The party will also try its hand in the panchayat elections this time. Instead of bringing Nishant directly to power, preparations are being made to first bring him into the organisation. When father became CM for the 10th time, Nishant took blessings by touching his feet Nitish Kumar became the Chief Minister of Bihar for the 10th time on November 20, 2025. After taking the oath as CM at Gandhi Maidan, Nitish Kumar reached the CM residence at 1, Anne Marg, where he met his son Nishant. An emotional picture of both emerged from here. Nishant touches his father Nitish Kumar's feet, while Nitish Kumar embraces him.

stories.title: Goons point pistol at gateman to open railway crossing:Pose as Crime Branch officers; train kept honking in Mainpuri
stories.summary: Seven youths travelling in two cars pointed a pistol at a gateman in Mainpuri after he refused to open a railway crossing. They threatened to kill him, abused him, and beat him badly with slaps and kicks. They even tried to lift him and drag him towards their car while assaulting him. The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed at the railway crossing. The accused claimed to be Crime Branch officers. The gateman kept pleading, saying a train was about to arrive and that he could not open the gate. He warned that an accident could occur and asked who would be responsible, but the attackers did not listen. During the assault, two colleagues of the gateman were also seen trying to intervene. The attackers created chaos at the railway crossing for around 20 minutes. Because of this, the Kalindi Express remained halted on the track for about 15 minutes, continuously blowing its horn. The incident took place on the night of February 2, about 2 km from Tindoli railway station. The CCTV video surfaced on Wednesday. Police have registered an FIR against five unidentified persons. See the youth's hooliganism in CCTV footage, 3 pictures... CCTV cameras installed at the railway crossing clearly show that the gate was closed. From the other side, seven men get down from a Tata Sumo and another car. Two youths wearing grey and blue blazers take out pistols from their waist and move towards the gate cabin. They press the pistols against the gateman standing there and start abusing him, ordering him to open the gate immediately. When he refuses, the youths punch the gateman in the face and then try to lift him and drag him towards their car. Near the crossing, they beat him brutally with kicks and punches. Two colleagues of the gateman are seen trying to intervene. All the youths are seen carrying pistols tucked into their waists. The incident is reported to have occurred around 1:25 AM on February 2, 2026. The Tindauli railway crossing, which is about 15 kilometres away from the district headquarters and just 1-2 kilometres from the nearby Tindauli railway station, had its gates closed at that time due to the passing of the Kalindi Express. During this time, a Tata Sumo and another car stopped near the crossing. 5-6 people got out of the car, who were carrying weapons. Identifying themselves as Crime Branch officers, they entered directly into the gateman's cabin and started pressuring him to open the gate. When gateman Awadh Kishore refused to open the gate before the train passed by, citing rules, the alleged policemen lost control. Abuse, pushing, shoving, and fighting broke out. It is alleged that one person directly pointed a pistol, while the others stood with weapons at their waists. Track patrolling man expressed fear Track patrolling man Narayan Singh, who was on night patrol at the time of the incident, also reached the spot. He said, "We were on night patrol. The gate was closed for the Kalindi Express. Just then, 5-6 people got out of a car and entered the cabin. They started abusing the gatekeeper and asked to open the gate. When refused, they assaulted and pointed a pistol." According to Narayan Singh, all the people were armed, and they crossed all limits of misbehaviour with railway employees. Train halted for 15 minutes, area echoes with horn Due to the show of force, railway clearance could not be given. The Kalindi Express remained halted at the railway crossing for around 10 to 15 minutes and kept blowing its horn continuously. The sound of the horn echoed through the area in the silence of the night, creating panic among locals. Railway staff said that even a small mistake could have led to a major rail accident. Police statement: Case registered, probe underway Dannahar police station in-charge Virendra Pal Singh said that a case has been registered in the matter and an investigation has been started based on the viral video. He said strict action will be taken against those responsible. However, it is still not clear whether the armed men were actually police personnel or imposters posing as police.

stories.title: Teachers beat 10 students in Kanpur college:Students assaulted with belts and sticks for arriving late, girls injured; 4 teachers arrested, protests follow
stories.summary: Kanpur’s Maharana Pratap Engineering College witnessed chaos on Wednesday morning. Teachers allegedly chased and beat students with sticks and belts for arriving late. Ten students, including four girls, were injured. One girl’s hand was cut, and seeing her bleeding, fellow students became enraged and protested. The college gates were closed, and students began shouting slogans like “We want justice.” Some property in the college was also damaged. Injured students were admitted to the college hospital. As the protest escalated, police and PAC forces were called. Authorities calmed the students and ended the protest. Following a complaint by a student’s father, a case was filed against three teachers. The college administration suspended two teachers, and police arrested four teachers. College management accepted students' demands The management has closed the college for three days; it will reopen on Monday. Students have warned that any action against them on Monday will trigger another protest, for which the college administration will be responsible. Detailed account of the incident Maharana Pratap Engineering College, located on GT Road in Mandhana, offers professional courses. Classes start at 9 AM. On Wednesday, BBA, BCA, and BTech students arrived after 9 AM. It is alleged that students arriving late were beaten by teachers, who also closed the college gate. Students Abhishek, Chitransh, Krishna, Agrim Dwivedi, Akshansh, Asmit Sonkar, and girls Muskan, Anjali, Anshika, and Ananya were injured. Muskan’s hand was cut during the beating. Four injured girls were admitted to the college hospital. Students said the city was shrouded in heavy fog that morning, making visibility poor. They reached the college using their own resources and were technically late. Students protest inside the college After late students were beaten, teachers closed another gate, leaving other students outside. When students asked for entry, they were refused, leading to a confrontation. Angry teachers reportedly came out with sticks and started hitting students at the gate. Other students inside the classrooms witnessed this, rushed out, and began chanting slogans. The protest quickly escalated into chaos. Students said they informed the Bithoor police station as the protest grew. They explained that they were blocked at the gate and beaten. When they protested, teachers started hitting them with sticks. Police and administration step in Seeing the chaos, the college management suspended Assistant Professors Subhash Chandra Maurya (Computer Science Engineering) and Anil Kumar Pathak (Electrical Engineering). An inquiry committee was formed. Wednesday’s classes were suspended, and students were asked to leave the campus safely. Four other teachers—Prashant Mishra, Shubham Goyanka, Rohit Verma, and Shivani Kapoor—were taken into police custody. Police met students and assured them that action would be taken. College gate closed, stopped outside After beating the late-arriving students, teachers closed the second gate. As a result, students who came later were stuck outside. When they asked for entry, they were denied. This led to an argument between teachers and students. The allegation is that some angry teachers arrived with sticks from inside and started beating students standing at the gate. When other students present in classes inside the college got this information, they became enraged. Coming out of class, they started shouting slogans. Within moments, the protests and commotion began to escalate. Seeing the increasing student protest, Bithoor police station was informed. Students told police that they were stopped at the gate for arriving late and then beaten. When they protested against the beating, the teacher started hitting them with sticks. 2 teachers suspended, four taken into police custody Seeing the students' protest escalate, the college management suspended Subhash Chandra Maurya, Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Engineering, and Anil Kumar Pathak, Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering. An inquiry committee has been formed to investigate the matter. Additionally, Wednesday's classes have also been suspended and students have been asked to safely exit the campus. Besides the two suspended teachers, four other teachers - Prashant Mishra, Shubham Goinka, Rohit Verma, and Shivani Kapoor - have been taken into police custody. Students say they were only 10 minutes late DCP, ADCP, and ACP were present at the site. Students said they were only 10 minutes late. Teachers, including Anil Pathak, began hitting students and charging Rs 300 as a late fee. Students alleged verbal abuse, illegal fines, and threats of being expelled. They warned that if no action is taken against the teachers, they would escalate the protest. During the protest, students locked the college gate. Complaint by student’s father Over a dozen complaints have been filed with ACP Kalyanpur. The father of victim student Akshansh Awasthi filed a case at Bithoor police station, stating that his son, a BBA first-year student, was unwell and yet beaten along with other students. Police registered a case against teachers Anil Pathak, Subhash Maurya, and Pankaj. Bithoor SHO Ashok Saroj said students are being spoken to and admitted that the protest is due to anger over the beating. Additional police forces were deployed to maintain control.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav slams Election Commission again:Claims BJP supporters are manipulating voter lists; says ignoring complaints from citizens across India
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav again criticised the Election Commission over the SIR process. He claimed that BJP supporters are influencing which votes are added or removed. He said complaints are being ignored and the Election Commission, a constitutional body, should focus on registering as many voters as possible. “The way the Commission is acting, it seems like it is working for the BJP,” he added. Akhilesh Yadav also criticised the recent deal with the United States, calling it a “concession” and saying it hands over India’s market to them. Akhilesh said - Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, George Fernandes, Netaji (Mulayam Singh Yadav), and all other socialist leaders always said that if we face the greatest threat from anyone, it is from China. Even the Rezang La Memorial, where it was built, was removed and rebuilt several kilometres away. SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav said on the non-functioning of the session- I have seen the tenures of many prime ministers from 1952 to 2014. But it was not suspended in this manner. Meanwhile, BJP MP Arun Govil from Meerut targeted Rahul Gandhi. He said- No amount of condemnation is enough for his behavior. Such behavior by an MP is very shameful.

stories.title: Room of 3 sisters who committed suicide:Walls full of pencil scribbles, cross marks, and emotional messages linked to Korean game
stories.summary: Scattered belongings, a picture of Radha-Krishna on the wall, pencil sketches at several places and cross marks drawn over them were found inside a flat in Ghaziabad’s Bharat City Society. Written alongside the sketches were emotional messages, including: “I am very alone” and “Make me a heart of broken”. This is the flat from where three minor sisters, Nishika (16), Prachi (14) and Pakhi (12), jumped to their deaths. Preliminary investigation suggests the sisters were deeply involved in an online game known as the “Korean Love Game” and were unable to come out of it. A Bhaskar reporter visited the two rooms of the flat from where the sisters jumped. The flat has three rooms, one where the sisters lived, one used by their father, and a third room that was vacant. The vacant room had a balcony attached, from where the girls jumped after placing a stool near it. The walls of this room had several pencil sketches, slogans and drawings. Many of these had cross marks drawn over them, indicating they were cancelled or rejected. In the room where the sisters lived, a family photograph was found pasted on the floor. The girls’ father, Chetan Gurjar, said his daughters often spoke about wanting to go to Korea. He said the online game involved 50 tasks, and Sunday was the final task. To complete it, the girls jumped from the ninth floor. According to the family, the middle sister played the role of a “death commander” in the game. This character reportedly assigned tasks to the other two sisters, who followed her instructions. The incident took place at flat number 907 in Bharat City’s B-1 Tower. Investigation into the role of the online game is ongoing. Picture of Radha-Krishna in the room, cross marks seen at several places The family lives in a 3BHK flat with three rooms and a hall. On entering the flat, the first room on the right is occupied by the girls’ father, Chetan, along with his two wives. The adjacent room was where all three sisters lived. The third room has a picture of Radha-Krishna. The door to the girls’ room was broken. According to the family, it had to be broken in haste after the incident. Inside, the room was found in complete disarray. The beds were unmade, the cupboard was open, and a picture of Radha-Krishna was also present. A banana plant had been planted inside the room as well. Several pencil marks and sketches were visible on the walls. In some places, cross marks were drawn over the sketches, suggesting that such marks were made after tasks were completed. A stool was found in the room. On inquiry, it was learned that all three girls had climbed onto this stool before jumping. Crying emoji in suicide note Police found a diary in the room where the three sisters used to sleep. A suicide note was written across 18 pages of the diary. According to the police, the note reads: “Mom, Dad, sorry… I can’t quit the game. Now you will realise how much we loved the game you wanted us to give up. Whatever is written here is true. Please read it. Really sorry. Sorry, Papa.” After this message, a crying emoji was also drawn in the diary. Police: Girls jumped from a height of 80 feet, all 3 sisters declared dead The three girls have been identified as Nishika (16), Prachi (14) and Pakhi (12). Their father, Chetan, is engaged in online share trading. Family members told Dainik Bhaskar that the girls had locked their room from the inside before the incident. Hearing a loud sound, the family rushed to the room and found the door locked. It was then broken open, after which the girls were not found inside. The family members immediately ran downstairs, where the girls were found lying injured. Superintendent of Police Atul Kumar Singh said the police received information at around 2:18 am and reached the spot soon after. All three girls were found in a critical condition and were taken by ambulance to the government hospital in Loni. Doctors there declared all three dead.

stories.title: Stray cow chases 3 in Chaupatiya:Girl thrown and gored by horns, dozens of stray animals in colony; Municipal Corporation helpless
stories.summary: In Lucknow’s Chaupatiya area, a cow violently attacked a young girl on 1 February, repeatedly throwing her to the ground. Before attacking the child, the same cow had already chased three people that day. Not just one, but dozens of cows and dogs roam freely across Chaupatiya. The municipal corporation appears helpless. Whenever the civic body’s team reaches the area to catch roaming animals, people who rear them start protesting. Following information about the cow attack on the child and the large number of stray animals, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached ground zero. In just two to three lanes, more than 15 cows were seen roaming. A large number of dogs were also present. The team spoke to the child’s grandmother and neighbours to understand the situation. Locals said that if people milk cows for livelihood, they should keep them tied inside their homes. In this report, read what residents and children have to say, the situation in Chaupatiya, and what action the municipal corporation has taken so far. Grandmother said - The girl is scared, not coming outside The injured child’s grandmother, Asha Rastogi, said that the child was going to a shop when a cow suddenly chased her. The cow kept attacking her repeatedly. Residents somehow managed to drive the cow away and brought the child home. Blood was coming out of the child’s mouth. She is badly traumatised and is not stepping out of the house. She said they only want people to keep their cows tied. “It is their livelihood, so no one comments, but animals must be restrained. Animals can attack anyone; someone could even lose their life.” The grandmother added that they do not want action against anyone, but people should keep their animals tied. Father said - Blood started coming from the girl's mouth The child’s father, Shailendra Malhotra, said stray animals are always seen roaming in the area. He demanded action from the municipal authorities. The grandmother said the incident took place at around 11.30 am on 1 February, when the cow became uncontrollable. The child suffered serious injuries and was bleeding from her mouth. She is currently undergoing treatment. “We feel our child narrowly escaped. That cow has attacked many people earlier as well,” the family said. Child says – had to abandon bicycle and run 7-year-old Sayan said he had to leave his bicycle and run when a cow chased him. “If the cow had hit me, it would have been over,” he said, demanding removal of cattle from the area. Local resident Mohammad Amanatullah said cows and dogs have created serious problems. Cow dung is scattered on the roads, causing inconvenience. He said complaints have been made several times and the problem needs to end. Sayan said, “If the cow had hit me, the story would have ended.” Action should be taken against those letting cattle roam Local resident Jitendra Agrawal said a cow became uncontrollable and ran at high speed, trampling the child. The child was saved with difficulty. He said such cattle must be controlled to prevent harm to others. Sharad Kumar said he was standing nearby when a cow suddenly charged. People shouted to save themselves. One person managed to escape, but the child got caught in the attack. Municipal Corporation officials said - Action will be taken now Municipal Corporation Animal Welfare Officer Dr Abhinav Verma said that injuries caused by animals left unattended in public places fall under public nuisance and also violate the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. Rearing animals without a licence is a punishable offence. Letting domesticated animals roam freely in the city is a serious crime. When the municipal corporation team reached Chaupatia for action after the matter came to light, people protested. The municipal corporation team's mobiles were snatched. They were also misbehaved with. The municipal corporation will file a case against the person who raises cows and leaves them on the road. Action is being taken against Mohammad Munna, Mohammad Raju and Mohammad Chhote Bhaiya for this.

stories.title: Consensual sex is not a crime, intent was not dishonest:Allahabad High Court quashes FIR, sets precedent in ‘false marriage promise’ cases
stories.summary: A girl from Noida took admission in a college in Jodhpur to pursue an LLM course. There, she met a young man. The two became friends, and the friendship gradually turned into a romantic relationship. Both decided that they would get married in the future. They started living together, during which they also had physical relations. Later, a dispute arose between the two over some issue and the relationship broke down. Following this, the woman lodged a rape case against the man. The matter reached the Allahabad High Court, where proceedings began and both sides presented their arguments. After hearing the case, the court rejected the woman’s allegation of rape. Several similar cases have also come before courts in the past, where similar observations have been made. What do courts say in cases alleging rape on the pretext of marriage? We try to understand the issue through these rulings. Court says there was no false promise of marriage The woman registered an FIR in Noida on 12 February 2024, accusing the man of rape on the pretext of marriage. She alleged that she was threatened, assaulted and that physical relations were established with her on the false promise of marriage under Section 69. Challenging the FIR, the accused approached the Allahabad High Court. The case was heard by a bench of Justice Siddharth Verma and Justice Abdul Shahid. The accused told the court that they got engaged in June 2023. The wedding date was fixed for 12 November 2024. After finalising the date, a hotel was booked, wedding cards were printed and even a photographer was hired. However, due to a mutual dispute at the last moment, the relationship broke down. After hearing both sides, the court made its observations. Commenting on Section 69, the court said that this offence is made out only when it is shown that from the very beginning the man had no intention of marrying the woman, made a false promise, and established physical relations on that basis. Since this was not the case here, the FIR under Section 69 was quashed. However, the allegations related to threats and assault will continue to be investigated. Judge said: woman herself responsible for rape Several cases involving consensual physical relations later being termed as rape have come before the High Court, on which strong remarks have been made. One such case also came from Noida, where the judge went to the extent of saying that the woman herself was responsible. In this case, on 23 September 2024, an MA student of a university in Noida lodged a rape complaint at the Sector-126 police station. She stated that she had gone to a party at Hauz Khas’s ‘The Record Room’ bar. Two female friends and three male friends were also present. During cross-examination, the defence raised the issue of the woman being an adult. The judge said that the complainant was an MA student and capable of understanding morality. The woman alleged that everyone partied and consumed alcohol till 3 am, after which she became intoxicated. She claimed that Nishchal asked her to accompany him, took her to a relative’s flat in Gurugram and raped her twice. Following the complaint, Nishchal was arrested and the matter reached the Allahabad High Court. From the accused’s side, it was argued that the complainant admitted she was an adult, willingly went to a party with male friends, consumed alcohol and stayed till 3 am. If these facts are accepted, it cannot be a case of rape but may amount to consensual relations. Justice Sanjay Singh observed that the complainant was an MA student and capable of understanding morality. If her own allegations are accepted, it can be concluded that she invited trouble herself and was responsible for it. Further, the medical report showed that the hymen was torn, but there were no signs of sexual violence or force. Therefore, the accused was granted bail. Supreme Court has also refused to term consensual relationships as rape Two months ago, a case came before the Supreme Court bench of Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice R Mahadevan. A woman had registered a rape case against a lawyer, alleging rape on the false promise of marriage. The Bombay High Court had convicted the lawyer. The accused challenged the verdict before the Supreme Court. In fact, the complainant woman had filed a case against her husband and was seeking maintenance. During this period, she became close to the appellant lawyer. From 2022 to 2024, both lived together for nearly three years. When the lawyer proposed marriage, the woman refused, citing ongoing disputes from her previous marriage. Later, she lodged the rape case. The appellant lawyer claimed that the woman had taken ₹1.5 lakh from him and registered the rape case only after he refused to give more money. He said that they lived together for three years and she never complained of sexual assault during that period. After hearing the case, Justice BV Nagarathna observed that the relationship between the woman and the lawyer was consensual. It was not a case where the appellant lured the complainant only for physical relations and then disappeared. The relationship lasted for three years, which is a considerable duration. The High Court had also failed to note that the FIR itself stated that the relationship was consensual. The Supreme Court said that while there are cases where trust is genuinely broken and women are wronged, allegations must be based on evidence and not anger or assumptions. With these observations, the court quashed the FIR and charge sheet registered under IPC Sections 376, 376(2)(n) and 507. When a married woman alleged rape on the promise of marriage Physical relations on promise of marriage not always a crime The Supreme Court has repeatedly commented on such cases. It has said that failure to fulfil a promise of marriage does not automatically amount to rape. What needs to be examined is whether the accused had dishonest intent from the very beginning. While analysing consent, the maturity, circumstances and evidence must be considered. The court has clarified two situations. If a person never intended to marry from the outset and knowingly made a false promise to establish physical relations, it would amount to a misconception of fact under Section 90 IPC and fall within the ambit of rape. On the other hand, if a person genuinely intended to marry but later could not do so due to certain reasons, it would be treated as a breach of promise and not a criminal offence. However, this must be supported by evidence. Lawyers say the law is often misused Legal experts say that not every case involves wrongdoing by men. Ajit Yadav, a lawyer at the Lucknow High Court, said that invoking rape provisions in such cases amounts to misuse of law. If a woman is an adult, she is capable of understanding what is right or wrong, and such cases cannot be termed as rape on false promise. He added that being misled applies in the case of minors. Here, the woman was an adult and an LLM student, capable of making decisions about her future. However, after a dispute, the law is sometimes used to harass the other party. According to him, the court’s decision is appropriate. Senior advocate Anil Kumar of the Allahabad High Court said that the law is flexible in favour of women. Once a complaint is made, the police are bound to register an FIR. The statement recorded under Section 164 CrPC becomes the basis for further action. Indian law gives priority to women, and police are required to act immediately on their complaints.

stories.title: Bikers shoot BJP leader in public:Returning from RSS event in Gorakhpur; known to be close to CM Yogi, active in Hindu Yuva Vahini
stories.summary: A BJP leader was shot by bike-borne attackers in Gorakhpur on Tuesday night. The bullet struck him in the back, causing him to collapse on the spot. Hearing the sound of gunfire, people in the area rushed to the scene. The attackers fled immediately after the firing. The incident took place in Bhainsaha village under the Gagaha police station area. The BJP leader was returning home after attending an RSS programme. Police said the attack appears to be linked to an old rivalry. Four youths are being searched for in connection with the case. The injured leader is considered close to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. He has previously served as district vice-president of the Hindu Yuva Vahini and is also the manager of an intermediate college. Police first shifted the injured BJP leader to the Community Health Centre (CHC). From there, he was referred to the district hospital, where he is currently undergoing treatment. Police have inspected the crime scene and launched a search operation to trace the accused. Full details of the case The injured leader has been identified as Radha Mohan Singh, a resident of Bhainsaha village. He has earlier served as district vice-president of the Hindu Yuva Vahini and is the manager of Leelawati Singh Smarak Intermediate College. Along with his association with HYV, he has remained active in the BJP. Radha Mohan Singh is counted among those close to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. His family includes his father, wife, a younger brother, a son and two daughters. According to family members, he had gone to attend an RSS programme on Tuesday. At around 8.45 pm, he was returning home. The route near the Kaithwaliya embankment is said to be deserted and poorly lit. Police said the attackers were already lying in wait in the area. As soon as he reached the spot, they opened fire. The bullet hit him in the back, and he fell to the ground. After the firing, the attackers fled. Hearing the gunshot, villagers rushed to the scene and informed the police. On receiving information, police reached the spot and immediately shifted him to the hospital. Crowd gathers at hospital After news of the shooting spread, a large number of people gathered at the Community Health Centre. Considering the seriousness of his condition, doctors referred him to the district hospital. He remains under medical care. Old rivalry suspected Police said the attack may be linked to an old rivalry in the village. In 2023, cases were registered against some local youths for allegedly harassing college-going girls. The BJP leader had lodged the complaint, following which the accused were sent to jail. After their release, tensions between them reportedly increased. Four attackers suspected During questioning, the BJP leader said he suspects four youths were involved in the attack due to the old rivalry. He also claimed to have identified two of the attackers. Police teams are continuing raids to trace the accused.

stories.title: Instructors’ jobs safe in Uttar Pradesh:Supreme Court rules no job loss; clears way for ₹17,000 honorarium payment
stories.summary: The jobs of about 25,000 part-time teachers (instructors) who have been working in Uttar Pradesh for years will not be terminated. The way for their honorarium of 17,000 rupees has also been cleared. The Supreme Court has dismissed the state government's appeal, in which the UP government was against increasing the honorarium of instructors. The Supreme Court's double bench has clearly stated that the appointment of instructors cannot be considered merely contractual even after the expiry of the stipulated contractual period. This decision of the Supreme Court has brought direct relief to teachers who have been demanding an increase in honorarium since around 2013. The Supreme Court said in its order that part-time teachers were kept on the job even after the expiry of the stipulated contractual period and were also prevented from taking up other jobs. In such a situation, this appointment is no longer merely contractual. The court held that in these circumstances, such posts would be deemed to have been created automatically, and the government cannot evade responsibility by calling them temporary. State government's appeal dismissed, teachers win The Supreme Court, completely dismissing the state government's appeal, stated that part-time teachers have suffered injustice for years. This decision by the court is considered a major legal victory for thousands of instructors and part-time teachers in Uttar Pradesh. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's order, affirming the decision to provide the full benefit of a honorarium of 17,000. Supreme Court asked - What is the problem in increasing the honorarium? In this case related to the honorarium of instructors, a detailed hearing of about three hours took place in the Supreme Court on Tuesday. A double bench of Justice Pankaj Mithal and Justice Prasanna B. Varale reserved the judgment, directing the state government and the petitioners to file a written reply within three days. The court's observations seemed to create a favorable atmosphere for the instructors. During the hearing, the Supreme Court asked tough questions to the state government. The Court said, Only when India learns, will India progress. What is the problem in giving you an honorarium? The state government's lawyer also agreed with this remark by the Court, which further strengthened the hopes of the instructors. ?7,000 Honorarium Since 2013, Court Deems It Unfair Labor Practice The Court also made strong remarks against the state government regarding the 7,000 per month honorarium fixed in 2013. The double bench stated that keeping the honorarium fixed for such a long time without any revision falls under the category of unfair labor practice. Part-time teachers are continuously providing services, and thus, they cannot be deprived of respectable remuneration. The Supreme Court clarified that part-time teachers working in Uttar Pradesh are fully entitled to the revision of the honorarium fixed in 2013. The Court stated that the revision of the honorarium should be done at regular intervals, and if not possible, then at least annually. The order also stated that from 201718, the honorarium for part-time teachers will be considered 17,000 per month, which will remain effective until the next revision. Payment from april 1, 2026, order to clear arrears in 6 months The double bench ordered that the payment of the revised honorarium should commence from April 1, 2026. It was also directed that the entire arrears of part-time teachers must be paid within a period of six months from today, i.e., February 4, 2026. Honorarium doubled in 2017, not implemented The honorarium of instructors working in the Basic Education Department of Uttar Pradesh was increased from Rs 8,470 to Rs 17,000 in the year 2017. However, after the change of government, this decision was not implemented. In protest against this, the instructors filed a petition in the Lucknow High Court bench. The then Justice Rajesh Singh Chauhan of the single bench of Lucknow High Court had ordered to pay the instructors an honorarium of Rs 17,000 with 9 percent interest. The state government filed an appeal challenging this order. The double bench of the High Court directed the payment of Rs 17,000 honorarium for only one year, after which the matter reached the Supreme Court. Debate concluded in Supreme Court after 2 years After an interval of about 2 years, the hearing of this case was completed in the Supreme Court. Senior advocates Sakharam Yadav, PS Patwalia, and Durga Tiwari presented a strong case on behalf of the instructors. Chief petitioner Ashutosh Shukla, Rakesh Patel, and other petitioners were also present during the hearing. Brijesh Tripathi, legal advisor to the instructors, stated that the Supreme Court's decision coming in favor of the instructors is a big victory.

stories.title: 15 policemen pose as farmers in Ghaziabad, catch inspector:Roamed for 2 hours with applications; raise alarm as soon as he takes ₹50,000 bribe
stories.summary: A shocking case of alleged bribery has come to light at Niwari Police Station in Ghaziabad. On February 3 at around 12:15 PM, the Station House Officer (SHO) Jaipal Singh Rawat was caught red-handed by the Meerut Vigilance team while allegedly accepting a bribe inside his office. According to information, the SHO was listening to public complaints in his office when four people suddenly entered the room. All of them were wrapped in shawls and had their faces covered. The SHO recognised one of them and asked the complainants to wait outside. One of the men then took out a bundle of Rs 500 notes from inside his shawl and placed it on the table. He told the SHO that it was Rs 50,000 and asked him to count it. The SHO reportedly replied that the amount was complete and put the money into his right pant pocket. Soon after, around 13 to 14 people present in the police station removed their shawls. They were earlier believed to be farmers, but were actually officers from the Meerut Vigilance Department. When three of them entered the SHO’s room, he appeared nervous and asked them to leave. The gunner standing outside also tried to push them out. At this point, one of the officers showed his identity card. This led to chaos inside the police station as it became clear that the Vigilance team had conducted a raid. The SHO was taken out of his own police station like an accused. The Vigilance team seized the bribe money and registered a case against him. As the SHO was in uniform, he was not arrested immediately. His plain clothes were called from home. A case under the Prevention of Corruption Act has now been registered, and an investigation into disproportionate assets has begun. The Vigilance team later took the SHO from Ghaziabad to Meerut for further action. Vigilance team arrived in 3 vehicles, parked 100 meters before This raid began on Tuesday morning at 10 AM. Inspector (SHO) Jaipal Singh Rawat of Niwari police station in Ghaziabad was listening to complaints in his office. A sub-inspector and 3 constables were also moving around in uniform in the police station, and the clerk was writing something in a file in his room. 3 cars stop 100 meters before the police station gate. From this car, Inspector Krishanveer Singh of the Vigilance team alighted and checked if anyone was at the police station gate. He was accompanied by a team of 15 people, who were in plain clothes. Constable Anuj was wearing a shirt and had a shawl draped over him. He entered the police station and asked the constable on guard, "My mobile phone has been stolen, whom should I meet?" The constable said, "Inspector sir is busy inside, you write your application. Then give it to the clerk in the room opposite; he will stamp it and return it to you." In this way, one by one, all the Vigilance constables entered the police station as complainants. Some started writing applications, and some started explaining their neighbor's dispute to the police. One of these constables sent a message to Vigilance Inspector Krishanveer on his mobile that the SHO is in the room. The clerk is getting signatures on postal documents. As soon as the money was taken, one signal, everyone nabbed the inspector. After this, Krishnaveer, DSP Azad Singh and Inspector Bhupendra Singh reached the police station. With them was former Pradhan Rakesh Kumar, from whom the SHO was demanding a bribe of 50 thousand rupees. The former Pradhan told the guard constable - Inspector Sahab has called, the constable went inside and informed about the former Pradhan. The inspector thought that the former Pradhan must have brought the money. Then everyone was allowed to go inside the room. Everyone had covered themselves with sheets and wrapped mufflers around their heads. The former head entered the inspector's room and said- Sir, as you instructed, I have brought the full amount Saying this, he placed the wad of notes on the inspector's table. The inspector asked- How much is it? The former head said- Count it, it's all there. The inspector smiled and put the money in his right pant pocket. After this, everyone came out. Then a signal was given, and all the vigilance personnel present at the police station removed their shawls and mufflers. The vigilance team, who were posing as complainants, entered the inspector's room. The inspector, flustered, said- Who are you Get out! Seeing this, the gunman deployed for the inspector's security started to flee from there. After this, the team introduced themselves. A staff member from the Ghaziabad DM office is also with the team, who tells the police officers the reality that this is all a trap. After this, his clothes are ordered from the inspector's residence. He is told to take off his uniform and wear plain clothes. An FIR was lodged against the inspector at his own police station. Then, dressed in plain clothes, he was dragged like an accused and made to sit in a car. The team has taken him to the Vigilance Office in Meerut, and further interrogation will now take place. It is also being said that the inspector's assets will be investigated. Inspector used to deal with money himself Jaipal Singh Rawat, a resident of Pauri Garhwal, Uttarakhand, joined as a constable in 1996, then served as a head constable. He became a sub-inspector in the civil police after passing an exam in 2013. After this, he was posted in Hapur. Two years ago, after being promoted to Inspector, he was posted at Niwari police station in Ghaziabad. According to the police station staff, the inspector used to deal with money matters himself. People would come to meet him at his police station residence from 7 AM, and he would decide who should be booked at the police station and who should be sent to jail. It also came to light in the vigilance investigation that the former headman, who gave a bribe of 50 thousand, has a bank branch below his house, from where the generator battery was stolen. Thieves who came in a white car were also visible in the CCTV. The former headman submitted an application at the police station, but the inspector did not register a case of theft. On February 3, when the vigilance searched the police station office, this application was also found under the table. FIR was filed against the former head on January 2 Rakesh Kumar alias Bittu, who lives in Abupur village, was the head of the village till 2005. The former head's wife is a government teacher in Hapur's Hafizpur. The former head said - On January 2, 2026, the police registered a case against me. This case was filed against me by Vijay Singh, alleging that I made indecent remarks against the CM and PM. The incident was shown at 4 PM on the 2nd, at that time I was in SBI bank. I said that my location should be checked. CCTV should be checked. I did not write anything in any group. I have an electoral rivalry with Vijay Singh from my village. A case has been filed against me as part of a conspiracy. After this, Inspector Jaipal Rawat came to my village. He said - I will send you to jail, otherwise give 50 thousand rupees. An FIR has been filed. I kept pleading, but he did not agree. After this, he complained to police officers in Ghaziabad. But no help was received from anywhere. Then Rakesh Kumar sought help from Meerut Vigilance.

stories.title: ‘Sorry, Papa, we could not quit mobile games’:3 sisters aged 12, 14 and 16 leave suicide note before jumping from 9th floor in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, three biological sisters committed suicide by jumping from the ninth-floor balcony. According to the police, at around 2 AM on Tuesday, the three locked the room from inside, placed a stool, and jumped one by one from the balcony. The girls were approximately 12, 14, and 16 years old. Their father said that all three daughters were addicted to a task-based Korean love game. They stayed together all the time, bathing and going to the toilet together. Their addiction was so severe that they had even stopped attending school. Media reports claim that the father had forbidden them from playing the game and scolded them. Because of this, the sisters took this step. In the room where the three girls slept, the police found a diary. Eighteen pages of the diary contained a suicide note. According to the police, the note read, “Mom-Dad, sorry… I cannot quit the game. Now you will realise how much we loved the game, which you wanted us to give up.” The incident took place at Flat Number 907, India City B-1 Tower. Additional Police Commissioner for Law and Order, Alok Priyadarshi, said that the investigation so far indicates that all three committed suicide. They used to play the game on their mobile phones. The circumstances leading to their suicide are still under investigation.. Additional Police Commissioner (Law and Order) Alok Priyadarshi says,The police are investigating all aspects of the case. So far, the probe suggests that all three died by suicide. They were living together and used to play games on their mobile phones. The police are looking into the circumstances that led them to take this step. Police Say Girls Jumped from 80 Feet The three girls have been identified as Nishika (16), Prachi (14) and Pakhi (12). Their father, Chetan, works in online share trading. The family consisted of the mother, a son, and the three daughters. The flat where they lived had two rooms and a hall. At the time of the incident, the husband and wife were sleeping with their son. The girls were asleep in the other room. The family told Dainik Bhaskar that the daughters first locked the room from inside and then jumped. “We heard a noise and ran. We saw the room was locked. Then we broke the door and found the girls were not there. We ran downstairs and saw the girls lying on the ground,” they said. SP Atul Kumar Singh said the police received information at 2:18 am and reached the spot immediately. The girls had jumped from a height of 80 feet. They were found lying on the ground, seriously injured. All three were taken by ambulance to Loni Government Hospital, where doctors declared them dead. Father says: “They had been playing games for three years, often saying they wanted to go to Korea” Father Chetan revealed that his daughters had written, “Sorry Papa, we could not leave the game. The Korean game is our life, our world.” He said, “The daughters had been playing games for three years. They had not been attending school for the past two years. They played games all day long. They did not talk to people around them. They often said that they wanted to go to Korea.” ‘Middle daughter gave tasks, the other two followed’ Chetan said, “Sometimes when we went into their room, all three would move to another room. Daughter Prachi would give tasks to the other two. She played the role of the game character Death Commander. The other two daughters would follow everything she said. All three daughters were together all the time. They would go to the toilet together and even bathed together.”

stories.title: Contract killer Banarasi Yadav killed in encounter in Kashi:Hired for ₹5 lakh to kill real estate businessman; 18th criminal shot dead in 125 days
stories.summary: A wanted criminal involved in a major contract killing was shot dead in a police encounter in Varanasi late on Tuesday night. The Special Task Force took action after receiving specific intelligence about his location. Late at night, the STF team surrounded Banarasi Yadav on Chaubepur Road. The inspector asked him to surrender, but he opened fire instead. Two bullets passed very close to two constables, who narrowly escaped without injury. Police encounter details After this, the STF team returned fire and moved forward. There was a direct exchange of about five rounds of firing. Banarasi Yadav was hit by two bullets and fell to the ground. He was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Two pistols and live cartridges were recovered from the spot. Banarasi Yadav was a resident of Karanda in Ghazipur district. He had 21 criminal cases registered against him, including 10 murder cases, in districts such as Varanasi and Ghazipur. Contract killing background Police said Banarasi Yadav had taken a contract to kill a real estate businessman in Varanasi. Five months ago, Yogendra, a property dealer from Ghazipur, allegedly planned the murder over land worth around ₹50 crore and paid Banarasi Yadav ₹5 lakh. Banarasi later hired three shooters, including former soldier Arvind Yadav and another criminal named Vishal. On August 21, 2025, the coloniser Mahendra Gautam was shot dead in broad daylight while he was going to his office. After the murder, police had announced a reward of ₹1 lakh on Banarasi Yadav. Officials said the encounter has now closed the case. Expert in changing appearance, did not use mobile phone Banarsi Yadav was counted among the big and cunning shooters of Purvanchal. The police knew Banarsi by name, who committed murders for hire, but no one had his face or picture. This was the reason why Banarsi remained out of police grasp even after committing several incidents. Banarasi Yadav never used a mobile phone and never stayed in one place. He was also adept at changing his appearance. After the murder of colonizer Mahendra in Sarnath, when Banarasi Yadav's name came to light, the police got a solid clue about his presence. After much investigation, his picture emerged. Since then, the police had been searching for Banarasi Yadav. Colonizer shot from a moving bike in broad daylight

stories.title: Swatantra Dev–Brijbhushan clash sparks BJP tension in UP:Kurmi vs Lodhi caste battle escalates over water scheme failures, raising questions on IAS accountability role
stories.summary: Brother, roads are dug up everywhere. Every village head is facing problems. There has been massive negligence in the Har Ghar Nal scheme. What answer do I give to the people? said Brijbhushan Rajput, Charkhari MLA I am ready to visit 40 villages. Providing water is our responsibility. Officers are with me. If roads are dug up and water isn’t supplied, I will suspend the officials. said Swatantra Dev Singh, Jal Shakti Minister Clash in Mahoba turns political—and social A confrontation between BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput and Uttar Pradesh Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh on January 30 in Mahoba district has now snowballed into a larger political and social controversy. What began as a dispute over delays and alleged irregularities in the Har Ghar Nal Scheme is increasingly being framed, on social media and at the grassroots, as a Kurmi vs Lodhi caste conflict, raising serious concerns for the BJP. Rajput belongs to the Lodhi community, while Minister Singh is from the Kurmi community. The growing perception of a caste-based power struggle has put the ruling party on edge. What exactly happened on January 30? On January 30, Swatantra Dev Singh arrived in Mahoba for an official program. As he was leaving, his convoy was stopped by Charkhari MLA Brijbhushan Rajput, accompanied by over 100 village heads (gram pradhans). Their complaint: The situation escalated into a heated exchange between the minister and the MLA. Social media fuels the fire Soon after the incident, social media pages linked to Swatantra Sena began targeting Brijbhushan Rajput. Leaders and youth from the Kurmi community accused the MLA of political grandstanding. In response, Rajput’s supporters and Lodhi youth launched counterattacks, accusing the minister of administrative failure. What was initially a governance issue soon took the shape of a caste-based confrontation, further complicating matters for the BJP. Why BJP is worried The BJP has reportedly received feedback that both communities linked to the two leaders are feeling aggrieved. Notably, no party notice has been issued to Brijbhushan Rajput even five days after he blocked the minister’s convoy—an unusual restraint that reflects the party’s caution. According to sources, BJP state general secretary Dharmpal Singh spoke to Rajput to understand the issue. The MLA told him he had written multiple letters to the minister earlier, but no improvement occurred in the scheme’s implementation. The party fears that if this episode goes unchecked, other MLAs may start publicly confronting ministers, setting a dangerous precedent. Lodhi discontent already simmering The Lodhi community is considered a key BJP vote bank in Uttar Pradesh. Leaders like Animal Husbandry Minister Dharmpal Singh and Union Minister BL Verma were contenders for the BJP state president’s post. However, the party appointed Pankaj Chaudhary, from the Kurmi community, as state president. This had already caused dissatisfaction among Lodhi leaders. The current controversy has further deepened that resentment, potentially impacting the BJP’s electoral base if not resolved swiftly. BJP collects ground feedback The BJP leadership is now actively gathering ground-level feedback. Social media trends and posts related to the controversy are being closely monitored. Local leaders have been instructed to help defuse tensions and prevent the issue from escalating further. No intervention yet from CM or State president Senior party leaders believe the issue requires direct intervention. Many feel that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and State BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary should bring both leaders to the table and resolve the dispute amicably. What political analysts say Senior journalist Anand Rai believes MLAs do have accountability toward their constituencies, but the protest could have been handled differently. “It would have been better if the MLA had spoken to the minister behind closed doors. Stopping a minister publicly may be a style of protest, but it should have been done within limits. As for caste conflict, Kurmi and Lodhi communities have not historically been at odds.” Another senior journalist, Ratan Manilal, points to deeper governance issues. “Complaints against ministers have increased. Earlier, only opposition leaders raised questions; now, BJP MLAs and office-bearers are doing so. Blocking ministers signals the need for changes in governance. If this continues, it will become difficult for the government. This dispute is now turning into a caste conflict on social media.” Will action be taken against both? A BJP office-bearer revealed that the party is treading cautiously. Recently, State President Pankaj Chaudhary faced backlash after issuing a one-sided warning to Brahmin MLAs. “That’s why the party wants to avoid unilateral action. If any action is taken, it will have to be against both the minister and the MLA. For now, the party is trying to let the matter cool down gradually.” Another critical angle: Are officials not responsible? Jal Jeevan mission lagging behind Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, the target was to provide tap water to every household in UP by 2024. However, due to slow progress, deadlines have been repeatedly pushed forward. Despite this, senior officials from the Additional Chief Secretary to engineers have remained in the same departments for years. While the Rajput–Singh clash grabbed headlines, dozens of Bundelkhand MLAs have written complaint letters to the government regarding irregularities in the project. Allegations of large-scale irregularities MLA Brijbhushan Rajput claims he has been writing to the minister and principal secretary for two years, alleging a major scam in the Har Ghar Nal scheme. He has raised the issue in the Assembly and demanded a CBI probe, alleging that: He also challenged the district administration’s claims, saying that even 50% of the work has not been completed in many areas. He demanded accountability, including resignation, if officials’ claims are found false. Officials under the scanner 1. Anurag Srivastava 2. Rajashekhar The bigger question As political tensions rise and caste narratives sharpen, a crucial question remains unanswered: Will accountability stop at political leaders, or will senior bureaucrats also be held responsible for delays and alleged irregularities in one of UP’s most ambitious welfare schemes?

stories.title: Poet Munawwar Rana’s daughter alleges dowry torture:Says, 'Husband issued triple talaq abandoned family'
stories.summary: Famous poet Munawwar Rana’s daughter has filed a case alleging triple talaq and dowry harassment. The complainant, Hiba Rana, has accused her husband and in-laws of demanding dowry, subjecting her to physical abuse, and later issuing triple talaq. An FIR has been registered at Saadatganj police station in Lucknow. According to the complaint, Hiba Rana was married to Syed Mohammad Sakib, a resident of Sakirye House in Karimganj, on December 19, 2013. She alleged that soon after the nikah, her in-laws began demanding dowry. When the demands were not fulfilled, she was allegedly assaulted and forced out of the house. Not allowed to take children: Hiba Rana Hiba further claimed that she was not allowed to take both of her children with her while being expelled from the matrimonial home. However, when Dainik Bhaskar contacted Munawwar Rana’s other daughter, Sumaiya Rana, regarding the allegations, she declined to confirm the claims. She stated that there was “nothing of this sort” and did not elaborate further. ‘They demanded ₹20 Lakh and flat’ Hiba Rana alleged that at the time of her wedding, her family gave gold and diamond jewellery along with ₹10 lakh in cash as dowry. However, soon after she reached her matrimonial home, her husband Syed Mohammad Sakib and father-in-law allegedly began demanding additional dowry. According to Hiba, the fresh demands included ₹20 lakh in cash and a flat. She claimed that her family fulfilled these demands on several occasions in an attempt to save her marriage, but despite this, the harassment and pressure for dowry continued unabated. Thrown out after triple talaq Hiba stated that on April 9, 2025, her husband allegedly abused and brutally assaulted her. When her sister, Arshia Rana (Tina), arrived at the house to meet her, the situation worsened. Hiba alleged that her husband became more aggressive and pronounced triple talaq. She further claimed that after divorcing her verbally, her husband pushed her out of the house and locked her children—son Syed Fawaz and daughter Hayyam Fatima—inside a room. Police officials said that the case has been registered based on the complaint and that the matter is currently under investigation. Further action will be taken after the probe is completed.
