stories.title: MLA blocks drain, water floods 20,000 homes in Lucknow:Locals claim severe waterlogging, visible structural damage to tiles and homes
stories.summary: In Lucknow’s Khargapur area, blocking of a drain is causing water to accumulate in empty plots. Nearby houses are developing dampness, and tiles are coming loose. To protect their homes, residents are dumping concrete debris against the outer walls to strengthen the foundations. Homeowners opposing this are being threatened with demolition. Repeated complaints were made to Mayor Sushma Kharkwal, MLA Yogesh Shukla, Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar, and councillor Mamta Rawat, but no solution has been found. To understand the residents’ problems, Dainik Bhaskar visited the ground zero. Locals accused Subhaspa MLA Bedi Ram of blocking the drain, while MLA Bedi Ram has outright denied the allegations. Encroachment on drain land In Khargapur, near Bharwara Malhaur Ward, on the road from Amity University towards the STP, the MLA has extended about 6 feet to build a boundary wall on the drain land. This has narrowed the drain, preventing wastewater from flowing out. As a result, dirty water is filling nearby empty plots and colonies. During the monsoon, the situation becomes severe. This is the drain that is supposed to be constructed. MLA Bedi Ram is accused of encroaching on it. Here’s what the locals said… Reena said – 20,000 homes affected Reena said that water from this drain goes to 20,000 homes, but the MLA has blocked the drain by occupying its land. Because of this, water is entering their houses. Even when municipal trucks came to take action, the MLA did not allow any work. Ranju said – Water and drainage problems Ranju said that the water and drainage issues are severe. Bathroom and house tiles are coming loose. During rains, water enters homes. Drain water is flowing into houses, and people are falling ill. Vibha Singh said – Drain blocked, no relief Vibha Singh said that there is no outlet for water. Residents are struggling with illnesses. The drain has been blocked ahead. From the Mayor to the MLA, assurances were given, but no one is listening. Men and women in Khargapur are distressed due to the situation. Demolition threats for homes Ram Vijay said that the drain has been closed for the past year. Water is entering plots and houses in the colony. Residents have been unable to sleep for over a year. Some try to open it, some close it. Fights are breaking out among locals. They meet the Mayor and municipal officials every week. They are being threatened that the entire colony is illegal and homes will be demolished. Until one and a half years ago, the drain went straight from the STP to the river. Water from over 2,000 homes used to flow through it. Now, sewage water is entering homes. Mayor and then Municipal Commissioner Indrajeet Singh also visited the site, but nothing changed. MLA says – Thousands facing difficulties Local BKT MLA Yogesh Shukla inspected the site on Saturday, accompanied by municipal officers. The MLA said the drain will eventually be dug. Locals are facing problems. He added that water used to flow freely before, and no one could stop it. As elected representatives, responsibilities increase, but now the entire population is suffering from waterlogging. At the site, councillor Mamta Rawat and her supporters accused revenue officer Kaushal of malpractice. Mayor says – Encroachment will be acted upon Mayor Sushma Kharkwal said that anyone occupying government land, regardless of position, will face action. About a year ago, she visited the site after complaints, when residents reported that 30,000–40,000 people were affected due to one person. She asked the MLA to show legal papers for the encroached land, but nothing has been done so far. About a year ago, Mayor Kharkwal had visited the site to inspect the encroachment after residents’ complaints. MLA says – Drain land will be measured MLA Bedi Ram rejected the allegations entirely, saying that the drain land will be properly measured and only lawful actions will follow. He explained that he owns a marriage lawn, and revenue officers repeatedly visit taking money. He also raised the issue in the assembly and demanded answers. He added that he will talk to the Mayor and Municipal Commissioner, as municipal officers and revenue officials are not working according to government directives. “We have not used any abusive language,” he said.

stories.title: Lucknow goldsmith absconds with nearly 1-kg gold:Gold from Bahraich jeweller was sent from Aminabad to Chowk; police register FIR
stories.summary: In Lucknow’s Chowk area, a craftsman absconded with 967 grams of gold entrusted to him by a jeweller from Bahraich. The accused’s mobile has been switched off since the incident. The victim filed a case at Chowk police station. Manthan Patil (32), a gold and silver trader from Kajipura North in Bahraich, said that on February 6 he sent jewellery craftsman Afzal Ahmed to Lucknow along with his employee Shivaji Bhosle. Afzal was instructed to collect gold from a jeweller in Aminabad and deliver it directly to Shani Verma, operator of New Balaji Ornament, in Chowk Sarafa Market. Alone in Aminabad According to Manthan Patil, Afzal Ahmed deliberately left Shivaji Bhosle waiting in the Chowk Sarafa Market and went alone to Aminabad. There, he collected 967 grams of fine gold and sent only a photo of the gold to the trader on WhatsApp to create an illusion. After this, Afzal reached Chowk but intentionally avoided going to the shop, heading instead towards the parking area. He then switched off his mobile and fled with the gold. After waiting for a long time without any trace, the suspicion of theft intensified. Chowk police have registered a case based on the complaint. The authorities stated that CCTV footage is being examined and a search for the accused is ongoing.

stories.title: Lucknow man duped of ₹7.12 lakh in trading scam:Cyber scammers displayed fake ₹1 crore IPO profit and wanted ₹20 lakh deposit to withdraw funds
stories.summary: Cyber fraudsters in Lucknow tricked a young man into investing in share trading and IPOs by promising huge profits, swindling him of several lakh rupees. Following the victim’s complaint, a case has been registered at Gudamba police station, and an investigation is underway. According to Mayank Srivastava, a resident of Shyam Enclave, Janakipuram, he received a call on 8–9 December inviting him to join a WhatsApp group related to trading. After joining the group, the fraudsters helped him open a trading account and initially made him deposit ₹5,000. The next day, a profit was shown in the account, which gained their trust. Victim asked to deposit ₹20 lakh to withdraw funds Subsequently, the victim was persuaded to deposit a total of ₹7,12,500 in installments across different bank accounts. The scammers promised investment in an IPO and displayed a fake profit of ₹1 crore in his account. When he asked to withdraw the money, they demanded an additional ₹20 lakh deposit. Suspecting fraud, the victim contacted SEBI, which confirmed that he had been cheated. He then filed a complaint on the 1930 Cyber Helpline, resulting in ₹3,47,000 being frozen across the bank accounts used by the fraudsters. The victim stated that the WhatsApp group was called “Steady Hain Group,” administered by a person named Kavya Godbole. Account manager Raghavan Narayanan handled communications. Full details of the bank accounts used in the scam have been handed over to the police. Gudamba police confirmed that a case has been registered based on the complaint, and the cyber cell is identifying the accounts and suspects. Action against the accused will follow soon.

Near Bhimsen railway station, unidentified individuals threw stones at the train’s First AC coach, shattering a window. The incident caused panic among passengers, and a video of the broken glass was released. Train number 20415, the Kashi Mahakal Express, was travelling from Varanasi to Indore. The incident occurred around 9 pm after the train departed Govindpuri station and approached Bhimsen. Following the incident, the coach attendant removed the broken glass. Bhimsen GRP station in-charge confirmed that an FIR has been registered against unknown individuals, and investigations are ongoing to trace the suspects.

stories.title: Father of three commits suicide over blackmail in Gorakhpur:AI-generated obscene videos used to grab property; FIR filed against five accused
stories.summary: A father of three, troubled by blackmail, hanged himself at his home in Gorakhpur’s Gorakhnath area. Before his death, he wrote a letter naming five people as responsible for his death. Based on this, the police have filed an FIR against the five accused under serious sections of law. All the accused are residents of the same colony as the deceased, Surendra Singh (50). In his letter, Surendra Singh named Rajesh Jaiswal, Rajkumar Yadav, Umesh Jaiswal, Dinesh Jaiswal, and Anil Chauhan of Vikas Nagar Colony as those who blackmailed him. The suicide occurred on 1 February 2026. An FIR was registered on Sunday evening following a complaint by the deceased’s son, Avinash Singh, and the Gorakhnath police are investigating. It is alleged that the accused created obscene videos using AI to blackmail him. Harassment drove father to suicide at home Vikas Nagar resident Avinash Singh stated in his complaint that Rajesh Jaiswal, Rajkumar Yadav, Umesh Jaiswal, Dinesh Jaiswal, and Anil Chauhan, all residents of the colony, have criminal tendencies. He alleged that the accused conspired to harass his father, Surendra Singh, for a long time because they wanted to seize his house. To do this, they created AI-generated obscene videos of his father and continuously blackmailed him with them. On 1 February 2026, around 6 pm, troubled by the blackmail, his father committed suicide at home. The family then informed the Gorakhnath police. During the investigation, the police recovered a letter in which Surendra Singh held all the accused responsible for his death. The letter was seized by the police. Avinash also stated that the accused had assaulted his father multiple times, and the persistent harassment had left him desperate. Letter written one month ago Police investigations revealed that the letter recovered from Surendra Singh was written about a month before his death. He had kept it with him for some time but had not formally complained anywhere. The accused used to visit frequently, causing ongoing tension. Became indebted trying to get son released from Nepal jail Surendra Singh worked as a clerk in a thread factory in the fertiliser sector. He had three married sons: Abhishek Singh, Avinash Singh, and Akash Singh. One of his sons had been arrested in Nepal in a theft case a year ago and has remained in jail there since. Sources say that in attempts to secure his son’s release, Surendra Singh borrowed money from multiple people. Many would visit his home to demand repayment, often leading to arguments. Among the accused in the case, Surendra Singh had also borrowed money from all five, and due to financial difficulties, he could not repay them. The accused allegedly wanted to seize his house and continuously pressured him to register the property in their name. His debts also prevented him from lodging any official complaints. Gorakhnath police station in-charge Vijay Pratap Singh stated that an FIR has been registered based on the complaint. Further investigation is ongoing, and action will be taken based on evidence.

stories.title: Baby girl burnt alive in Kanpur hospital warmer machine:Severe burns on face and stomach; NICU fire sparks anger among family members
stories.summary: A tragic incident took place at a private hospital in Kanpur on Sunday evening, where a newborn baby girl died after a fire broke out in a warmer machine inside the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). According to the family, the fire started suddenly while the baby was admitted to the NICU at Raja Nursing Home in the Brahmanagar area of Bithoor. The baby was badly burnt in the incident. Her face, chest, stomach and thighs suffered severe burns, and her body turned black due to the fire. She could not be saved. The family alleged serious negligence by the hospital staff. Angry relatives created a ruckus at the hospital after the incident. The baby’s aunt later filed a complaint against the hospital at the Bithoor police station. Police said the matter was being investigated. Hospital staff kept the incident hidden for 5 hours Arun Nishad, a resident of Bakarganj, works in a private company. In his family, he has his wife, Bittu. Arun Nishad said - On Sunday morning, his wife experienced labor pain. They brought her to Raja Hospital. The doctor suggested an operation. Around 4 PM, after the operation, Bittu gave birth to a daughter. This was Bittu's first child. The doctors shifted the wife to the ward. The daughter was admitted to the hospital's NICU. Late in the evening, the warmer machine in the NICU, where the baby was lying, caught fire. The baby died on the spot due to burns. For four to five hours, the hospital staff kept this incident hidden. Father said - Hospital should be closed, action should be taken against the entire staff Father Arun Nishad said - When we asked to show the child, the staff talked about admitting her. Late in the evening, we repeatedly asked them to show our daughter. When we got angry, the staff told us about the incident. This accident happened due to the negligence of the hospital staff. The hospital authorities are responsible for my daughter's death. The hospital should be closed. Action should be taken against the entire staff. As the commotion grew, we informed the police. Hospital offered 2 lakh to suppress the matter The relatives created a ruckus after the child's death. At this, the hospital management started to appease them. The relatives claim that the management offered a bribe of 2 lakh rupees to hush up the matter. Upon hearing the price for this innocent life lost due to negligence, the family members became even more enraged. Upon receiving information, the police arrived at the scene and calmed everyone down by assuring action. Mother said - could not see the child alive The baby's grandmother, Prema, said - I was anxious to see my granddaughter. I was happy that Lakshmi had come to my house. But, she had fallen victim to negligence. The system and staff of those who are called gods on earth took the baby's life. The mother could not even hold her baby alive to her chest. I don't have the courage to tell her how her daughter was burned alive. ACMO said - investigation team will respond in 24 hours ACMO Ramit Rastogi said - A 3-member team has been formed to investigate the incident. A response has been sought from the team within 24 hours. The hospital is registered, the cause of such an incident will be investigated and action will be taken. Bithoor Police Station in-charge Ashok Saroj said - We are talking to the family members. The newborn baby girl was admitted to the NICU. The baby was seriously burnt due to the fire in the NICU. This led to her death. A case will be registered and action will be taken.

stories.title: Asif posed as Ritesh marries Hindu woman:Victim alleges forced conversion, attempts to feed meat, sexual assault, and abandonment; police ignore complaints
stories.summary: A young woman living in Lucknow’s Saadatganj area has levelled serious allegations against her husband, claiming that Mohammad Asif married her by posing as Ritesh Kumar Maurya and later forced her to convert her religion. In a video released by the woman, she alleged that Asif took her to his home district Hardoi, forcibly converted her to Islam, changed her Hindu name to a Muslim one, and also gave Muslim names to their daughters. She claimed that Islamic rules were imposed on her against her will and that she was sexually assaulted when she resisted. The woman further alleged that she was forced to eat meat and that her brother-in-law attempted to rape her. She said her husband later abandoned her after coming into contact with another woman. At present, she is living in Lucknow with her two-year-old daughter. She claimed she filed complaints at Madeyganj, Saadatganj and Thakurganj police stations, but no action was taken as her husband allegedly bribed the police. The woman has demanded strict action against her husband and in-laws, appealing to the state government and police administration to ensure justice. ‘Police took no action on my complaint,’ says victim The victim said the police failed to act despite repeated complaints. She then urged people to watch her video to understand the full sequence of events. The woman released a 1 minute 55 second video in which she said she is originally from Kannauj and was born into a Brahmin family. She claimed that her father had given her in adoption to a friend from the Gupta family. After her adoptive father’s death, she came into contact with a man who introduced himself as Ritesh Maurya. She said he married her at an Arya Samaj temple in Lucknow’s Purania area following Hindu rituals and regularly accompanied her to temples, taking part in prayers. According to the woman, everything remained normal for about two years, during which their daughter was born. Later, the man revealed that he was not Hindu but Muslim, and that his real name was Mohammad Asif. She alleged that the marriage was part of a well-planned conspiracy. Forcibly converted religion with help of family members The woman alleged that Asif took her to Hardoi, where he and his family forced her to convert to Islam, threatening to kill her or throw her out of the house if she refused. With no relatives or family support, she said she was compelled to accept their demands. She claimed that her in-laws made her recite Islamic prayers, forced her to wear a burqa, pressured her to offer namaz, and changed her name to Shafia Bano. After the conversion, Asif brought her back to Lucknow, where she gave birth to two more daughters. She alleged that all three daughters were given Muslim names. About ten years later, Asif left her and started living with another woman. The woman said - My husband tried hard to corrupt my religion. He tried to make me eat meat. He committed atrocities against me. My brother-in-law tried to rape me. I complained at Madeyaganj, Saadatganj and Thakurganj police stations. He bribed the police officers. Because of this, no action was taken against him. Seized car and bike bought with father's money The victim further alleged that her in-laws kept her two elder daughters with them and also took possession of a car and bike purchased using her father’s savings. She said she is now struggling to survive with her two-year-old daughter and is wandering from place to place seeking justice, but no one is listening to her.

stories.title: Bijnor coldest in UP at 8°C:Temperature to rise by up to 3°C from tomorrow, fog likely to clear; 3-day alert issued
stories.summary: A dense fog alert was issued for 19 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Monday morning, affecting visibility in many areas. Strong winds kept the weather cold during the early hours, adding to the chill. Weather officials said the fog situation in the state is now easing. With no active weather system expected for the next two to three days, temperatures are likely to rise gradually. Atul Kumar Singh, a scientist at the Zonal Meteorological Centre, said the impact of fog has almost ended across Uttar Pradesh. He added that due to clear conditions, the temperature may increase by 2 to 3 degrees from Tuesday. On Sunday, Bijnor recorded the lowest temperature in the state. The minimum temperature there dropped to 8 degrees Celsius, making it the coldest district. Know today's alert See 2 pictures from Sunday- Know what the weather will be like for the next three days Risk of damage to mustard, potato, pea crops Amidst the severe cold, the effect of hail and rain is visible on the Rabi crops. This weather is good for the wheat crop. Mustard, potato, and pea crops are at risk of diseases. Scientists say that if there is an outbreak of pests and diseases, treat them immediately. Spray medicine only when the weather is clear. The effect of cold will end by the end of February In the month of February, the temperature has gradually started to rise. With the arrival of spring, the effect of cold also starts to decrease. According to meteorologist Mahesh Palawat, the temperature in February can increase by 3 to 5 degrees Celsius. However, this relief is not going to last long. Occasionally, due to western disturbances, a temporary drop in temperature can also be observed. Despite this, by the end of February, winter will completely depart from UP. How will February be for farming? According to Prof. P.K. Singh, a scientist from the Agriculture Department of BHU, February's weather is generally considered favorable for wheat crops. However, the weather is not favourable for pulse crops. There is a possibility of rain and hailstorms due to the influence of Western Disturbances. P.K. Singh says - If there is rain and a hailstorm, the growth of wheat may be affected. Whereas, pulse and other crops will be at risk of damage. Also, if frost occurs after rain, it can particularly affect potato and pea crops. This could lead to losses for farmers.

stories.title: Neither scooters nor relief for outsourced workers in UP Budget:Still waiting for expressway to AI City, big budget promises remain incomplete
stories.summary: UP Finance Minister Suresh Khanna presented the budget for fiscal year 2025-26 on February 20, 2025. In the budget of Rs 8,08,736 crores, Rs 28,478.34 crores were allocated for new schemes. Big announcements were made and promises were made to accelerate development. Now the budget for fiscal year 2026-27 is to be presented in the assembly on February 11, but the important announcements made by the state's BJP government in the past year have not yet materialized on the ground. Today read about the budget announcements that were not fulfilled... Outsourced employees' honorarium not increased The state government had announced to increase the honorarium of outsourced employees from Rs 16,000 to Rs 18,000. It was claimed that about 1.99 lakh contract employees of the state would benefit from this. The government had also announced the formation of a corporation for recruitment of outsourced employees. Its proposal has been passed by the cabinet. The corporation has also been formed. Amrita Soni has been made the MD (Managing Director) of the corporation. But the corporation has not yet started functioning. Therefore, the honorarium of outsourced employees has also not been increased. Girls did not receive scooters Finance Minister Suresh Khanna had announced in the budget to give scooters to meritorious daughters. The government had made a provision of 400 crores in the budget for this. More than 500 meritorious daughters, who secured top 10 positions at district and state level in the Intermediate Board results announced after last year's budget are still waiting to receive scooters. Textile and Leather Parks not built in 10 districts The state government had announced the establishment of Sant Kabir Textile Parks and Sant Ravidas Leather Parks in 10 districts, but so far neither have all the textile parks been built in all districts nor has the establishment of leather parks been completed. The process of establishing leather footwear parks in Kanpur and Agra is already underway with the support of the central government. Meanwhile, the Sant Kabir Textile and Apparel Park is being constructed on 75 acres of land in the Ramna area of Varanasi. According to MSME Minister Rakesh Sachan, action has begun for textile parks in Mau, Khemai (Aligarh), Chunar (Mirzapur), and Raebareli, while the remaining districts have not yet received financial approval. AI city also not built The state government had initiated efforts to develop the state as a hub in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI). For this, there was an announcement to establish an Artificial Intelligence City in Lucknow. A new Technology Research Translation Park in Cyber Security was included in the budget plan. The plans for AI City and Cyber Security Technology Research Translation Park are also only existing on paper. No plan ready for expressway The government had promised to build four new expressways. The first expressway was to go from Agra-Lucknow Expressway to Hardoi and Farrukhabad connecting with Ganga Expressway. The second proposal was to connect Ganga Expressway to Sonbhadra via Prayagraj, Mirzapur, Varanasi and Chandauli. The third was the expressway extension from Meerut to Haridwar. The fourth was a plan to build an expressway from Bundelkhand to Rewa. UPDA ACEO Hari Pratap Shahi said that the Rewa proposal has been cancelled. The tender process for Hardoi to Farrukhabad is underway. Land acquisition is in progress. Work is underway on the alignment for the Meerut-Haridwar Expressway extension. Action is being taken at the alignment level to extend the Ganga Expressway through Mirzapur, Varanasi, Chandauli up to Sonbhadra. It may take more than a year for ground work to begin on all four projects. Home Guards and Gram Chaukidars did not receive insurance The state government had announced in the budget to provide free treatment up to Rs 5 lakh under the Chief Minister Jan Arogya Abhiyan to Home Guards, PRD jawans, Gram Chowkidars, Shiksha Mitras, instructors of Basic Education Department and employees working on honorarium. Recently, the government has approved cashless insurance scheme for Shiksha Mitras and instructors from the cabinet, but insurance facility could not be implemented for Home Guards, village chowkidars and PRD jawans yet. Labor worker stations also not built The government had announced in the budget to build labor worker stations in all districts. These are to be provided with facilities including canteen, drinking water, bathrooms and toilets among others. The construction of worker stations in districts has not yet begun. Sardar Patel District Economic Zone not established The government had announced the establishment of Sardar Patel District Economic Zones in each district, considering their characteristics and potential, named after the Iron Man who unified India. Different sectors were to be developed in different districts. Recently, the government passed a cabinet proposal for this, but no park has been established in any district yet.

stories.title: Hybrid marijuana worth ₹30.94 lakh seized in Vapi:Accused from UP arrested, total seizure valued at ₹31.58 Lakh
stories.summary: Dungra police have arrested a youth from Uttar Pradesh with hybrid cannabis worth ₹30.94 lakh from the Balitha area of Vapi taluka. In total, goods valued at ₹31.58 lakh were seized during the operation. Acting on a tip-off, the police conducted a raid and apprehended Princekumar Premchandra Maurya, a resident of Balitha, Vapi, originally from Amethi, Uttar Pradesh. Authorities recovered 884 grams of hybrid cannabis from his possession, with an estimated market value of ₹30,94,000. The seized items include hybrid cannabis worth ₹30,94,000, cash of ₹8,000, two mobile phones valued at ₹5,500, a Hero Maestro scooter worth ₹50,000, along with weighing scales and transparent plastic bags. Police investigations have revealed that the main supplier behind this drug network is Surajsingh Pramodsingh from Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh, who has been declared wanted. Dungra Police have registered a case against Princekumar Premchandra Maurya under Sections 8(c), 20(b)(ii)(A), and 29 of the NDPS Act, and further investigation is ongoing.

stories.title: Rinku Singh to marry Priya Saroj in June:Wedding ceremony to take place in Kashi; couple engaged on 8 June last year
stories.summary: India's star finisher Rinku Singh and Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj are set to exchange marriage vows in June this year. The wedding will take place in Kashi. Rinku and Priya held their ring ceremony in Lucknow last year, on 8 June. A wedding date was initially fixed for November 2025, but it could not take place. A second date in February 2026 was also postponed due to the T20 World Cup and IPL schedule. The ceremony is now planned for June. Rinku’s elder brother, Sonu Singh, stated that the dates 11 and 12 June were initially considered, but due to Rinku’s IPL commitments, a new date was arranged. The wedding in Kashi will take place once Rinku is free from IPL matches, with the reception scheduled at Aligarh. Keeping politics away from the wedding From Rinku’s side, only about a dozen close family members and relatives are expected to attend the ceremony. The small guest list is deliberate: many of the groom’s close associates are linked to the BJP, while the bride herself is a Samajwadi Party MP. Invitations were therefore carefully considered to avoid any political tension. Following the ring ceremony, 20 MPs, including Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, Jaya Bachchan and Shivpal Yadav had given their blessings to the couple. During the ring ceremony on 8 June 2025, around 300 VIP guests attended the function , including BCCI Vice-President Rajeev Shukla, former cricketer Piyush Chawla, Praveen Kumar and bowler Yash Dayal. Arjun Singh Fakira, considered a mentor to Rinku, arrived in a car adorned with the BJP flag, which caused some objections from the Samajwadi Party side. Arjun Singh Fakira clarified that he parked the car outside before joining the ceremony. To avoid similar situations, the wedding in Kashi will have a small guest list, ensuring that political differences or rivalries do not become a source of dispute. Previous delays Fans have eagerly been awaiting Rinku and Priya’s wedding. Earlier dates were postponed: the first on 18 November 2025 was delayed due to a cricket series and the second in February 2026 was cancelled due to the World Cup. With the IPL final now concluded, preparations for the June wedding are underway. How Rinku and Priya met Their love story began around two years ago. During IPL 2023, Rinku hit five consecutive sixes to lead Kolkata Knight Riders to a last-over victory. Rinku became acquainted with Priya, who was introduced to him at a senior cricketer’s wedding in Delhi. Priya, a BA-LLB graduate from Delhi University, had been friends with the cricketer’s wife, which led to their introduction and the beginning of their relationship. About Priya Saroj Priya Saroj hails from Karkhiyanv in Pindra Tehsil, Varanasi district. Born on 23 November 1998, she joined the Samajwadi Party soon after turning 18 and actively participated in various party events. By age 25, she defeated BJP’s BP Saroj to win a Lok Sabha seat. Her father, Toofani Saroj, was a three-time MP from Machhlishahar (1999, 2004, 2009). Rinku Singh’s early life and cricket journey In an interview with KKR, Rinku spoke about his upbringing. He comes from a family of five brothers, with his father working in cylinder delivery. The brothers would assist him in deliveries, often transporting two cylinders per bike. Rinku began playing cricket with tennis and leather balls. He also played at Modern School in Aligarh, scoring 54 not out in an inter-school tournament off 32 balls. Initially, he could not afford club cricket fees and practised in government facilities with a membership card. Family support was limited: his father encouraged him to focus on studies, while his mother provided some assistance, even lending ₹1,000 from her shop for a nearby tournament.

stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, a plot of land valued at ₹10 crore in 2025 is now worth just over ₹3.2 crore in a year. Another property in the city, purchased ten years ago for ₹50 lakh, is now worth half its original value. These figures come from documents submitted with signature of a DIG-rank officer to his own department. This valuation concerns one of his properties. He remains the wealthiest IPS officer in Uttar Pradesh. Similarly, a SP who did not own a home until last year, has now bought a house in Rajasthan worth ₹3.40 crore with assistance from his brother and sister. Its value has appreciated by approximately ₹60 lakh in 12 months, bringing it to ₹4 crore. The central government had asked IAS and IPS officers to submit details of their assets to the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) by 31 January. IPS officers have now submitted their property declarations. Who owns what among IPS officers? The DIG of the Basti range is Sanjeev Tyagi. One of his properties alone has lost nearly ₹7 crore in value. Tyagi remains the wealthiest IPS officer in UP, with a total of five properties, worth around ₹30 crore. He purchased 0.838 hectares of land in Sadar, Ghaziabad, in 2010 for ₹40 lakh and spent ₹11 lakh on construction. In the 2025 asset declaration, he valued this land and property at ₹10 crore. However, in this year’s submission to the DoPT, he reported it at just ₹3.2 crore. Land value in Ghaziabad reduced by half in 11 years Tyagi owns another property in Modinagar, Ghaziabad, bought in 2015 for ₹50 lakh. This 0.356-hectare plot is now valued at ₹26 lakh, showing considerable decline in it's value in over 11 years. Sambhal SP Krishna Kumar buys ₹4 crore home Sambhal SP Krishna Kumar, who had not declared any property in 2025, reported a house purchased in Rajasthan in 2026 for ₹3.40 crore. Its current value is ₹4 crore. Purchased on 27 January last year, the house is jointly owned by his brother and sister and generates annual rental income of approximately ₹4.8 lakh. The property is also listed as mortgaged in official documents. Muzaffarnagar SP Sanjeev Suman sees land value rise 1.5 times in six months Similarly, Muzaffarnagar SP Sanjeev Suman, who had not declared any property last year, reported a plot in Lucknow purchased on 6 June 2025 for ₹20 lakh. Its value has increased to ₹30 lakh in just six months. IG Jhansi range and other officers’ properties Jhansi range IG Akash Kulhari purchased 240 square metres in Mohanlalganj, Lucknow, for ₹15 lakh last year. He also jointly owns a house in Jaipur with his brother. Another IG-rank officer, K. Aguilarson, posted in UP-112, owns 14 properties, up from 13 declared last year. Headquarters-level IPS officers’ holdings There has been little change among IPS officers in key headquarters positions. DG, ADG Law and Order, DG Fire Service, DG Jail, and ADG Railways officers’ assets remain largely unchanged from 2025. ADG zone officers’ properties in the field Among zone-level ADG officers, only Bhanu Bhaskar’s holdings have slightly changed. He declared six properties in 2026, down from seven in 2025. The most number of properties are held by Ramit Sharma (seven), followed by Bhanu Bhaskar and Jyoti Narayan (six each). Lucknow zone ADG Praveen Kumar has no declared properties. Police Commissionerate officers’ holdings In the police commissionerate, Jogendra Kumar holds nine properties, including inherited ones. Lucknow Police Commissioner Amarendra Sengar has five properties. Rakesh Prakash remains the largest landowner in the range Rakesh Prakash Singh continues to be the largest landowner in the range with 25 properties, mostly inherited. Most officers’ property holdings have not changed much compared to last year.

stories.title: I'll get you married, Chetan told eldest daughter:On the night of Ghaziabad triple suicide, father had lashed out at his 3 daughters, snatched their phones
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, three minor sisters committed suicide. Several theories are emerging around the incident. Initially, the focus was on an alleged addiction to a Korean game, but statements from the father have complicated the narrative. The absence of the children’s mother from public statements is also raising questions. Police investigations and questioning of family members so far indicate that the conflict began after the father scolded the daughters. When Chetan scolded the eldest daughter Nishika, she refused to eat dinner that night. Her parents attempted to calm her down. Afterwards, Nishika pretended to go to sleep along with her two younger sisters. Around 10 pm, Chetan went to sleep in a separate room with his third wife Tina. At that time, 16-year-old Nishika was given a mobile phone by her mother. Chetan lives in the flat with three wives Chetan (42) resides in Flat No. 907, B-1, Bharat City Society, Teelamod area, Ghaziabad, along with his family. His three wives are Sujata, Hina and Tina. Sujata and Hina are sisters, while Tina is Muslim. On the night of 3 February, Chetan’s three daughters—Nishika (16), Prachi (14) and Pakhi (12)—jumped from the ninth floor, committing suicide. Many speculations have arisen regarding the incident. Police questioned Chetan and all three wives. Statements revealed that around 8 pm on 3 February, Chetan scolded his eldest daughter Nishika. The girls reportedly jumped from the window of a room where they lived.. Mobile snatched, wife insulted when defending daughters In statements to police, Chetan and his wife said that the three sisters were interested in Korean boys on mobile phones. Angered, Chetan scolded Nishika and instructed her to slap herself. He then confiscated her phone and gave it to his first wife Sujata. Nishika complained to her mother. Chetan scolded her again, saying that he had warned her three days prior, had sold her phone, and would throw her to the ground if she used it again. The three daughters were reportedly scared of their father’s anger. Chetan also told his first wife Sujata and second wife Hina that they had spoiled the children with excessive love. He said he could not tolerate this behaviour continuously. When Sujata defended Nishika, Chetan verbally abused her. In anger, father told daughter: “I’ll get you married” Chetan reportedly told his eldest daughter Nishika in anger: “If you insist on behaving this way, I will get you married. I have already stopped you from going to school. I will marry you before you turn 18. No matter how much you use the mobile phone.” After this, Tina took Chetan to her room. On that night, Sujata prepared dinner around 8:30 pm, and Tina prepared a separate meal. At 9 pm, Nishika refused to eat and went to her room, covering herself with a blanket. The younger sisters, Prachi and Pakhi, also lay down with her under the blanket. Chetan confirmed scolding the daughters that night After scolding Nishika, Chetan reportedly argued with his wives Sujata and Tina. Both women said he only shouted and could have explained things calmly. Tina came out of her room, and the argument continued for some time. Nishika started crying. Chetan threatened her that if he had to slap her two more times, she would stay silent and also eat her meal. After about 10 minutes, Tina took Chetan to their room. A three-year-old child of Tina was also in the bed. Chetan then locked the door from inside. Mother Sujata gave Nishika a mobile phone After Chetan went to his room, everyone else in the family ate, but Nishika did not. Around 10 pm, Sujata gave Nishika her mobile phone. Nishika and her two younger sisters then lay down under the blanket again, using the phone. A seven-year-old boy was also on the bed with them. Meanwhile, Sujata and Hina lay on mattresses on the floor but did not sleep. Frustrated by Chetan’s behaviour, Sujata said he had ruined the entire household. She added that she and Hina were sisters, and that everything had been destroyed after Chetan married a Muslim woman as his third wife. Nishika gets up at 1 am to drink water Around 1 am, Nishika got up. Her sisters Prachi and Pakhi followed. Sujata asked where they were going. Nishika replied she did not even want water, then walked toward the temple room. The younger sisters followed. At some point, one of the girls brought in a plastic stool. Around 1:15 am, the three daughters locked the plywood door from inside. The mobile phone was with them. According to police, the girls were upset after being scolded by their father. They pretended to go for water and then committed suicide. Mother and father knocked on the door After some time, the daughters did not come out. Sujata woke Chetan. The couple tried to open the door. Around 2 am, the three daughters jumped from the window of the temple room. About two minutes later, Chetan and his two wives reached the spot via the lift, where they found the bodies of all three daughters. Arun, a resident of the opposite tower, told police that around 2 am he was on the balcony before going to sleep. He saw something unusual in the neighbouring flat: the three girls were seen falling, apparently being pulled slightly inside before they fell outside, and then they landed on the ground. One mobile of Nishika recovered DCP Nimish Patil said that Nishika’s father Chetan had previously sold two of her mobile phones. The phone recovered from the scene belonged to Chetan’s first wife Sujata. The girls had been using their mother’s phone for some days. The phone sold a few days earlier has been recovered from a shop and is intact. It will be sent to the forensic lab in Nivadi to check whether any data was deleted. Another phone sold six months ago has also been recovered.

stories.title: BJP MLA's nephew ends life in Lucknow:Body found hanging in flat; 'Not God, we will cause your downfall' instagram post emerges
stories.summary: The body of Shivam Tiwari, nephew of BJP MLA Vinay Kumar Dwivedi from Mehnoun assembly constituency of Gonda, was found in his flat in Lucknow. His body was hanging from a fan with the support of a bedsheet. Family members allege that Shivam's partners had committed fraud with him and embezzled money, due to which he had been troubled for many days. In this case, family members have filed a complaint against the accused partners at Sushant Golf City police station. About a week ago, on January 24, Shivam had also made a post on his Instagram account. Sharing a video of him working out at the gym, he wrote - "Not God, we will cause your downfall." The song playing in the background of the video was - "We are a different kind of people Bhakt ji. We don't leave everything to God's mercy. If you have wronged us, rest assured, not God but we will cause your downfall." Landlord broke down the door to enter Balrampur's Shivam Tiwari lived in a rented flat in Tower No. A2, Flat No. 407 at Rishta Manhattan in Sushant Golf City police station area. On the evening of February 1, the landlord arrived at the flat. Despite calling out for a long time, the door did not open. When the flat owner became suspicious, he called the security guard. Then while making a video, they broke down the flat's door, and upon going inside, found Shivam hanging from the fan with a noose. He immediately informed the police. When police arrived, family members were called. The body was brought down. Police said no suicide note was found at the scene. The body has been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. Was troubled over money matters The deceased's family members said that Shivam worked in property business. For quite some time, his business associates were not paying him money. Shivam had asked them for money several times, but there was no response from them. Due to this, Shivam was mentally very disturbed. Uncle is BJP MLA in Gonda Deceased Shivam Tiwari's uncle Vinay Kumar Dwivedi is a BJP MLA from Mehnoun assembly constituency of Gonda district. In the 2022 assembly elections, he won for the second consecutive time by defeating the SP candidate. Other members of Shivam's family have also contested MLC elections. Shivam's family includes father Rajesh Tiwari, mother, younger brother Prakhar and Abhishek. Family members have demanded filing of FIR against the accused partners.

stories.title: UP cabinet ministers clash publicly in Varanasi:OP Prakash criticises Anil Rajbhar's father; says, 'politics should not drag mothers into disputes'
stories.summary: 'If there is a shop selling votes anywhere in the country, let them tell us where. If anyone has the courage, let them speak up. Those who are pointing fingers today used to steal iron in the past. Has anyone done what Om Prakash Rajbhar has done in 23 years? When we started calling our father as father, only then did people's attention turn towards Suheldev Maharaj.'- Om Prakash Rajbhar 'OP Rajbhar used to drive an auto in Sindhora, Varanasi. Don't know when he came to our village to buy iron rods. You are calling all shopkeepers thieves. This is wrong. We remember that you never came to buy anything from our brother's shop. Why he is saying such things, only he knows.' - Anil Rajbhar These are statements from two cabinet ministers of UP government, who are currently at loggerheads with each other. Both ministers are in Varanasi on Monday. As soon as OP Rajbhar made his statement, Anil Rajbhar countered him after about 6 hours. First about OP Rajbhar's statement Called Anil Rajbhar and his father iron thieves OP Rajbhar became furious when questioned about Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar's statement. Without naming names, he called Anil Rajbhar and his father iron thieves. He said that you don't know their history. When his father was in politics, during this time he opened an iron rod selling shop. Any shopkeeper may claim to be honest, but he is not honest. If he becomes honest, how will he earn? If someone takes one quintal of iron rods and gives one quintal back, what will be left for him? OP Rajbhar said - We challenge that if a mother has fed milk, then tell us where votes are sold? We will also find out where the shop for buying and selling votes is? Let us also see that shop. If needed, we will sell our vote. Is a vote something in a sack or bag that can be handed over? Now read what Anil Rajbhar said Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar, who arrived in Varanasi on Monday evening, responded to OP Rajbhar's statements. Regarding the statement about drinking mother's milk, Anil Rajbhar said - Mother should not be dragged into politics. A mother is a mother. Whether she's yours or mine. It's not appropriate to challenge mother's milk. Our party's directive is to move forward with coalition partners. I hadn't named any party or leader. However, 10 to 15 people are sent drunk to disrupt our programs. We had those people removed. Now read what OP Rajbhar said On Shankaracharya - Country runs by Constitution, not by statements Om Prakash Rajbhar spoke openly about Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's statements. Said - the country runs by the Constitution. The Constitution cannot be changed by anyone's statements. On Shankaracharya's 40-day statement, he asked if he is the owner of 145 crore people? When the matter of giving state mother status to cow mother comes to the cabinet, it will be considered then. He called the Bareilly City Magistrate's resignation and meeting with Shankaracharya a drama and politics. Said that we are Rajbhars and speak boldly with pride. Said - UGC has not been withdrawn Om Prakash Rajbhar said - UGC has not been withdrawn, rather it has been stayed. Those who are protesting should tell that there were 17 people from general category in the UGC committee. Didn't they notice any shortcomings? Coding the Education Minister's statement, Rajbhar said that whatever shortcomings are there, they will be improved. Regarding UGC's new guidelines and laws, Rajbhar said - if anyone finds something wrong with this, the Supreme Court's doors are open. There is discrimination against OBC, SC and ST classes in the education system. We will fight for this. Rajbhar also taunted SP Taking a jibe at SP's PDA slogan, Rajbhar said that PDA means "Family Development Authority". Regarding the budget, he said that it has been made keeping in mind the interests of 145 crore citizens. The budget has been made for a developed India.

stories.title: Union Budget allocates ₹20,000 crore for UP Railways:Northern Railway DRM Sunil Kumar Verma says, 'Delhi–Kashi high-speed rail corridor approved'
stories.summary: Regarding the Union Budget, Northern Railway DRM Sunil Kumar Verma said that major approval has been granted for constructing a high-speed rail network in Uttar Pradesh. Under this decision, high-speed rail corridors connecting Varanasi with Delhi and Siliguri will be developed. Completion of these projects will not only save passengers’ time but also make travel between major religious, cultural, and economic centres of the state and the country much easier. Delhi to Kashi in just 4 hours DRM Sunil Kumar Verma stated that under the proposed high-speed rail project, the journey from Varanasi to Delhi will be completed in just four hours. At present, this journey takes around eight to ten hours. With the operation of high-speed trains, long-distance travel will become faster, safer, and more comfortable for passengers. Delhi–Varanasi corridor to span 865 kms The Railways will prepare a project of approximately 865 kilometres for the Delhi–Varanasi High-Speed Rail Corridor. This corridor will be based on state-of-the-art technology, including high-speed operations, advanced signalling systems, and strict safety standards to ensure reliable and secure travel. 2 major high-speed corridors linked to UP Out of the total newly announced high-speed rail corridors, two will be directly connected to Uttar Pradesh. The combined length of these two corridors is expected to be around 1,500 kilometres. Once completed, travel from Delhi to Kashi and towards eastern India will become significantly faster and smoother than before. Trains to operate at 300–350 kmph Trains running on the high-speed rail corridors will operate at speeds ranging from 300 to 350 kilometres per hour. This will save valuable time for passengers and bring a transformative change to long-distance rail travel across regions. The introduction of high-speed rail is also expected to reduce the growing pressure on roads and air traffic. A large number of passengers are likely to prefer fast and affordable rail services, which will help ease traffic congestion and reduce pressure on airfares. UP receives highest allocation of ₹20,000 crore Uttar Pradesh has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of this initiative. A budget allocation of approximately ₹20,000 crore has been made for the high-speed rail network in the state. This investment is expected to provide fresh momentum to infrastructure development, employment generation, and overall economic activity in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Boyfriend kills girlfriend, alters look by shaving head:Man brings woman from Mumbai, kills her brutally in Gorakhpur; wife supported him
stories.summary: Priya Shetty (35), a Mumbai resident, was murdered on January 30 and her body was dumped in Gorakhpur, police said. Her face was badly damaged with a brick and the body was stripped to prevent identification. Police arrested Priya’s boyfriend Vijay Kumar Sahni on February 2. Investigators said he strangled her, with his wife Sandhya also involved. Vijay shaved his head, beard and moustache to avoid CCTV identification, while his wife disposed of the clothes in a river. Despite this, police traced him through CCTV footage. He used his father-in-law Rambilas Sahni’s scooter during the crime, making him an accused as well. All three have been sent to jail. Senior police officers said a nude woman’s body was found under Barghatta bridge in Pipganj on January 30. Police launched an investigation using CCTV footage and surveillance to identify both the victim and the suspects. CCTV footage from the night showed three people riding a scooter, which raised suspicion. Tracing the vehicle led police to Vijay Sahni, who told investigators he works in the insurance sector and earns around ₹1.5 lakh a month. Police said Vijay had first met the victim, Priya Shetty, in 2012 during work-related interactions. Distance grew after having a son in live-in relationship Vijay told police that he and Priya grew close after a few meetings and began living together in a live-in relationship. He said they later married in a temple and had a son, who is now 13. After the child’s birth, relations soured and Vijay separated from Priya, also filing for divorce in a Mumbai court, which could not be completed as Priya changed her address. Vijay said he returned to Gorakhpur and married Sandhya in 2014. After moving back to Mumbai, Priya contacted him again through Instagram. He resumed meeting her and stayed away for long periods, during which his wife filed missing person complaints. Vijay said Priya later pressured him to take her home and threatened to create a scene, following which his family advised him to bring her to Gorakhpur to talk. Came to Gorakhpur from Mumbai on January 26 Vijay told police that on January 26 he reached Gorakhpur with his wife Sandhya and Priya Shetty and stayed in a hotel for two days, visiting local places. He said the three consumed alcohol frequently, and Priya often threatened to defame the family while drunk. He said that on the evening of January 29, they travelled by auto to Pipiganj after drinking. After an argument with the auto driver over fare, Vijay arranged a scooter belonging to his father-in-law. He claimed that while travelling towards Sahjanwa, the trio drank again, during which Priya created a scene and later collapsed in an intoxicated state, after which he and Sandhya put her on the scooter. Vijay said - I was driving the scooter. Priya was sitting in the middle and Sandhya was holding her from behind. Then we came across the Barghatta bridge on the way. We stopped the vehicle there and all three of us drank alcohol again. There too Priya started creating a scene. Then Sandhya said that she should be killed. At this, I quickly strangled Priya. Being intoxicated, she couldn't even scream. Vijay said that after killing her, along with his wife, he took her body 20 feet down from the bridge. There, to hide her identity, first crushed her face. After this, removed her clothes and made her nude. Then Sandhya and I went home and slept. The next morning, I went to the barber and got my hair and beard removed so that I couldn't be recognized. My wife had also thrown her clothes in the river. Police got help from auto driver SP Gyanendra Prasad said - The auto driver also played an important role in solving this case. After identification in CCTV, he was interrogated. He told that there was one young man and two women. This made it easier to identify the accused. Priya's son is in Mumbai. Her acquaintances have identified her. Now her post-mortem will be conducted. Morning walkers saw the dead body A nude body of a 35-year-old woman was found on the morning of January 30 (Friday) in the Pipiganj area of Gorakhpur. Police and forensic team arrived after receiving information. Evidence was collected from the scene. It was suspected that someone killed her and dumped the body here. The head was crushed to hide the identity. Additionally, injury marks were found at several other places on the body. People who went for morning walks under the Barghatta bridge in Pipiganj saw the woman's body. The woman's body did not have a single piece of clothing on it. The dog squad went to Bairghatta village climbing up the bridge from where the body was found. After about 200 meters, the dog returned. Signs of dragging were also found at some distance from the crime scene.

stories.title: Lok Sabha Speaker turned off Akhilesh's mic:'China issue is very sensitive; Rahul Gandhi should be allowed to speak' says Yadav
stories.summary: In the Lok Sabha, Speaker Om Birla turned off SP President Akhilesh Yadav's microphone. Akhilesh had stood up in support of Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi. He said - The China issue is very sensitive. If it's a matter related to national security, then Rahul Gandhi should be allowed to speak. Speaker Om Birla interrupted him on this. Akhilesh again rose from his seat. He said - I remember that Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, George Fernandes and Netaji (Mulayam Singh Yadav) always emphasized that we need to remain cautious of China. If we don't remain cautious of China, China has already occupied our lands. Akhilesh said - Open discussion in Parliament on important issues like national security and international relations is a fundamental requirement of democracy. It is necessary to hear the opposition's perspective so that correct facts and viewpoints can be presented before the country. Meanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav's microphone was turned off. However, the voices of other leaders sitting in the house could be heard. Rahul says - Chinese tanks were coming to Doklam, uproar in Lok Sabha Actually, Rahul Gandhi gave a speech in Lok Sabha on Monday during the motion of thanks on the President's address. He said Chinese tanks had reached India's border in Doklam. I am saying this with reference to a magazine article which quotes former Army Chief MM Naravane's book (memoir). Rahul said- Listen carefully to what I am reading, it will reveal who is patriotic and who is not. 4 Chinese tanks were coming onto Indian territory in Doklam. They were just 100 meters away. After this, first Defense Minister Rajnath Singh interrupted, then Speaker Om Birla insisted on placing the book in the house. Rajnath said - Let them (Rahul) tell if this book has been published or not. Don't mislead the house. The uproar over Rahul's speech continued for 46 minutes in the Lok Sabha. Speaker Om Birla interrupted him every time he spoke and cited the rules. Rajnath, Shah, Rijiju, and Nishikant Dubey were also seen opposing him. Naravane's autobiography 'Four Stars of Destiny' not published The book based on which Rahul Gandhi is claiming Chinese tanks entered Doklam in Parliament was written by former Army Chief General MM Naravane. This book titled 'Four Stars of Destiny' has not been published yet. It's hardcover is available on online shopping sites from April 2024. The book reviews the Indian Army's 2020 clashes with China along with the Agniveer scheme. Naravane, who served as Army Chief from 2019 to 2022, had told in an interview with Indian Express that he had given his book to Penguin Publisher Group for printing. Now this is a matter between the publishing group and the government. The book has been sent to the Ministry of Defense for approval. More than a year has passed but permission to publish it has not been granted. Imran Pratapgarhi asked - Why was that match played in Dubai after Operation Sindoor?

stories.title: Avimukteshwaranand says Ayodhya GST officer took embarrassing U-turn:Questions raised as beef shipped abroad as buffalo meat
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati on Wednesday mocked Ayodhya GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Singh for withdrawing his resignation. Laughingly, he said that after the Bareilly City Magistrate’s resignation, another “forced resignation” had now been taken back. He remarked that the officer had “licked back what he spat out” and claimed they had already predicted that the resignation would be withdrawn within four days — which is exactly what happened. GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar Singh had resigned on January 27 in support of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath but made a U-turn just four days later and withdrew his resignation. The officer later said that there was no pressure on him and that he was continuing to work normally. Avimukteshwaranand also hit back at Uttar Pradesh Animal Husbandry Minister Dharampal Singh over his remarks. He objected to the minister using the word “aaka”, saying it is an Arabic term and reflects a lack of understanding. He said that Shankaracharya is the highest spiritual position, above any administrative hierarchy. “A minister has a Chief Minister above him, and the Chief Minister has the Governor and Union ministers above him,” he said. The Shankaracharya added that the use of such language showed a “Mughal-like mindset”. This came two days after Dharampal Singh accused Avimukteshwaranand of spreading falsehoods about cow slaughter in Uttar Pradesh, claiming that the incidents cited were linked to the Shankaracharya’s own “superiors”. 'Ministers are misleading the public by making allegations against me' Shankaracharya got angry over the statements of ministers Om Prakash Rajbhar and Dharampal Singh Saini. Said- The government is claiming that only buffalo, goat and pork is exported from UP, not beef. However, pork is not exported from UP at all. Then on what basis is this claim being made. We want it to be clarified first how true is the talk of pork exports. If this is false, then there is no point in further discussion. Allegation of beef export under the guise of buffalo meat Shankaracharya alleged that cow meat is being continuously sent abroad under the name of buffalo meat. Referring to incidents in Noida and Bhopal, he said - initially the meat was claimed to be buffaloes, but in lab tests it turned out to be cow meat. When buffalo meat repeatedly turns out to be cow meat in investigations, how can government claims be trusted? Raised questions on number of slaughterhouses Shankaracharya also questioned the Yogi government's claim about shutting down illegal slaughterhouses. On this issue, he said - At the time when the Chief Minister took charge, there were about 40 processed meat exporting slaughterhouses in the state, which have now increased to more than 70 in 9 years. He asked - During whose tenure did this increase happen? If illegal slaughterhouses were closed, how did their numbers increase? Shankaracharya said - No sadhu, sanyasi or monastery head can be a meat seller. He alleged that the CM is taking salary from the treasury that receives income from meat exports. The Chief Minister's monthly salary of about four lakh rupees comes from the same treasury where money from meat sales is deposited. In 106 months, about four crore rupees have been taken as salary. Is this not an insult to saffron clothes and the sanyasi tradition? 'Questioning validity of Shankaracharya position shows ignorance' Responding to ministers calling the Shankaracharya position unconstitutional, Shankaracharya said - When the Shankaracharya tradition was established, the constitution did not even exist, but there were kings and they had given this honor. When the king gave us this position, throne and respect, today's governments are the successors of that system. Therefore, questioning the validity of the Shankaracharya position shows ignorance. He said in clear words - The position of Shankaracharya is not a gift of any modern constitution, rather this position is thousands of years older than the constitution. You cannot say that our position came from your constitution. This position has been continuing since before your constitution was even born. He also said that it is not Shankaracharya's work to make someone win or lose elections. Our work is to give right education to Sanatan Dharma followers. To save society from great sins like the killing of mother cow. If someone wins or loses by their own actions, how is that our fault? Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said that former Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, who resigned, met him late at night. However, as he was observing a vow of silence, no discussion took place. Agnihotri shared his views, the Shankaracharya listened and gave his blessings. The monks of the monastery honoured Agnihotri with a tilak and wished him success. Agnihotri spoke about protesting against the SC-ST Act, but the Shankaracharya could not ask questions due to his silence. Speaking on future plans, the Shankaracharya said he will write a letter to saints across the country. The letter will ask whether their Sanatan journey is on the right path or has gone astray. He said saints will be advised to stay away from meat traders and not trust anyone merely by saffron clothing, but to judge by conduct. He added that just as one checks the flow of milk or oil, people should look at actions, not appearances. What will happen to the Shivlings removed from Mahakumbh? On the question of removing the Shivling installed in Mahakumbh, Shankaracharya said - when the camp itself will not be there, why would the Shivling remain there. He informed that these Shivlings will now be installed in that temple where one and a quarter lakh Shivlings are to be consecrated. This temple is being built in Sapad Laksheshwar Dham (Saldha) on the banks of Shivganga river, Bemetara district of Chhattisgarh. The consecration of Shivlings will begin there on the occasion of Mahashivratri.

stories.title: Mute deaf children dance to bhajan:Premanand Maharaj watches with folded hands; kids ask, ‘How do we keep our courage?
stories.summary: Deaf and mute children from Kanpur met Premanand Maharaj in Vrindavan. They asked questions through their gestures. They danced to bhajans they had prepared themselves. During this time, Maharaj ji appeared immersed in the bhajan. He kept watching the children intently with folded hands. Actually, on Sunday evening, Manpreet Kaur, president of the Presidential Award-winning Divyang Development Society, arrived with the deaf and mute children. Manpreet said - These children cannot hear or speak. Some people call us crazy. They call us clever. What should we do so that our and the children's courage doesn't break? To this, Premanand Maharaj said that it is a matter of great fortune that you are nurturing such children. You deserve many thanks. Let selfish people say whatever they want. Your greatness lies in giving love and enthusiasm to such people, as you have accepted them leaving everyone else behind. 'Please bless us that our patience does not break' Manpreet Kaur said, ‘Maharaj ji, some people call us crazy, some call us clever. We are working in our own way. All the people who are associated with us are working in their own way. We just need your blessings that our patience should not break. May our courage remain intact.’ 'Your greatness lies in giving affection to such children' Premanand Maharaj said, 'It is a matter of great fortune that you are nurturing such children with motherly affection. You are also encouraging such children, otherwise such children become discouraged from life. You are worthy of much gratitude. Keep doing what you're doing. What do people know about all this? Everyone is selfish. You are walking the path of spiritual welfare. This is pure spiritual welfare. Because bringing enthusiasm in their minds, giving love to such ones, showing affection to them, this is your greatness. How to connect these children with spirituality? Manpreet Kaur asked - Maharaj ji, we are teaching these children. We are trying for their social upliftment. How do we connect these children with spirituality? Please give us that guidance. 'The heart will begin to purify through name chanting' Premanand Maharaj said - If they start chanting the name in any way, start remembering the Lord, meaning if it happens under your guidance. Radha, Radha, Radha... then their hearts will begin to become pure. They will begin to become sinless. Their auspiciousness will begin. Children sang - Are Man Le Chal Vrindavan... During this time, the children requested to present a bhajan in front of Maharaj ji. After getting Premanand Maharaj's consent, the children performed the bhajan. Adorned with flower garlands and kumkum like Radha-Krishna, the children sang - O mind, let's go to Vrindavan... O mind, let's go to Vrindavan Take me to the banks of Yamuna... Take me to Radha's feet O mind, let's go to Vrindavan... Bansivat... Shringar Vat and Keshi Ghat Want to talk to Radha, worship the dust... O mind, let's go to Vrindavan O mind, let's go to Yamuna's banks... Take me to Radha's feet. Watched children's dance attentively with folded hands Premanand ji was very happy seeing the children's performance. He listened to the bhajan attentively with folded hands. He said - it was a very beautiful presentation. Premanand Maharaj praised Manpreet Kaur for this kind of service and education of children. He blessed the organization's president and the children. Now the story of Sant Premanand Maharaj Left home at age 13 Premanand Maharaj was born in Akhri village of Narwal tehsil in Kanpur district of UP. His father is Shambhu Narayan Pandey and mother is Rama Devi. He has 3 brothers, Premanand is the middle one. In childhood, Premanand ji's name was Aniruddh Kumar Pandey. He was spiritual since childhood. He studied till class 8. In childhood, Aniruddh wanted to build a platform for a Shiva temple with his group of friends. He also started its construction, but some people stopped it. He became disappointed by this. His heart was so broken that he decided to leave home. He reached Kashi via Kanpur. When he turned 13, he decided to become a Brahmachari. Initially, Premanand Maharaj was named 'Aryan Brahmachari'. He spent about 15 months in Kashi. He received initiation from Guru Gauri Sharan Ji Maharaj. Then he came to Mathura. Premanand Maharaj transformed from a monk to a Radhavallabhi saint After reaching Vrindavan, Premanand Maharaj would visit Banke Bihari Ji daily. Then he started attending Raasleela and Radhavallabh programs. He would stand there for hours. One day a saint read a verse from Sri Radharassudhani, but Maharaj could not understand it. Then one day while circumambulating Vrindavan, he heard a sakhi singing a verse. Hearing it, Maharaj stopped in his tracks. The verse resonated so deeply that breaking his sannyasa dharma, he went to that sakhi. Asked her the meaning of the verse. The sakhi said - to understand its meaning, one must become a Radhavallabhi. This is how Maharaj became a Radhavallabhi.

stories.title: Naini Jail guard dies by hanging at home:Spoke to his fiancée last night ahead of wedding; body sent for postmortem, mobile seized, family informed
stories.summary: Prithviraj Chauhan, 26, who was posted as a jail guard at Naini Jail in Prayagraj, died by hanging himself at his private residence. He was originally from Ummanpur, Gohana, Mohammadabad in Mau district. According to jail sources, the incident occurred on Sunday night. He was soon to be married and had spoken to his fiancée for the last time. The body has been sent for postmortem. The family has been informed and is on their way to Prayagraj. So far, the investigation has not revealed the presence of any suicide note. Naini police have seized his mobile phone.

stories.title: Teacher aspirants clash with Lucknow police, scuffles erupt:Forcibly crammed into buses and banners torn after reaching Keshav Maurya’s residence
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a clash broke out between candidates of 69,000 teacher recruitment and the police during a protest. When their path was blocked, protesters got agitated. This led to pushing, shoving, and arguments. Police forcibly lifted the protesters and made them board buses. The demonstrators were crammed into buses and taken to Eco Garden. It is alleged that during this, the police also tore their banners. Protesters had arrived at the site around 11 am on Monday morning. One protester had a banner with slogans such as “I am unfortunate, backward, Dalit” and “Supreme Court is casteist.” Slogans were also written on the hands and bodies of the candidates. ‘Yogi rule is casteist, Supreme Court is casteist’ Candidates said: “I am unfortunate, backward, Dalit. The Supreme Court is casteist. Backward-Dalit reservations are being opposed, casteist Yogi rule prevails.” Using graphics, they explained that the Supreme Court gave a decision for 15% of upper-castes in a single day, while backward-Dalit candidates, who make up 85%, have been waiting 10 months with no decision. No progress has been made for reservation-category candidates in the 69,000 teacher recruitment. Protesters said that while a UGC decision was delivered in one day, the teacher recruitment matter has been stuck for 10 months. ‘We will come every day; let’s see how long police can stop us’ Amarendra, participating in the protest, said: “We will come every day and surround one by one every MLA, leader, and minister. Let’s see how long the police can stop us. We will fight this battle as long as we breathe. Om Prakash Rajbhar and Swami Prasad Maurya claim to be the biggest leaders of backward communities. If they were true leaders, why are children from backward castes being beaten?” “We have come to protest. Police are scared. They are cramming everyone into vehicles. These leaders and ministers are making police beat us and wield lathis. If our leaders had stood firmly, jobs would have been given by now. It is unfortunate that even in ongoing Supreme Court hearings, the government’s lawyer has not appeared.” News is being continuously updated...

stories.title: BSP leader’s Rottweiler attacks child in Hamirpur:Boy bitten on chest and arm, rushed to hospital; police probe, inquiry on dog's licence status
stories.summary: A Rottweiler dog owned by a BSP leader launched a life-threatening attack on a minor child in Hamirpur. The child fell to the ground as the dog attacked him, biting his hand and chest at four places and causing serious injuries. Hearing the child’s screams, the BSP leader rushed to the spot. The child was somehow rescued and immediately admitted to hospital. The 11-year-old had gone to the leader’s house to play with other children. He was coming down the stairs after playing on the terrace when the dog suddenly attacked him. The incident took place on Sunday night in the Sumerpur police station area. Police said a complaint has been received from the family. Preliminary inquiry has revealed that BSP Nagar President Shivam Janardan owns two Rottweiler dogs, neither of which is licensed. Know the full matter Rajendra Kumar Gautam, a resident of Sumerpur town, works in a steel mill. On Sunday evening, his son Ansh went to play at the BSP leader’s house, located about 50 metres away. He played on the terrace with his friend Pathik for around two hours. While returning home, the Rottweiler suddenly pounced on him. Ansh said he did not even get a chance to react. The dog bit him multiple times on his hand and chest. Hearing his cries, the BSP leader and family members reached the spot and rescued the child, but by then he had suffered serious injuries. The injured child was rushed to the Sumerpur Community Health Centre for treatment. Father said - Police did not take action even after complaint The victim’s father Rajendra Kumar said he submitted a written complaint against neighbour Shivam Janardan, but no action has been taken so far. Police said the matter is under investigation based on the complaint. Don't be careless if a dog bites Dr Rohit Bhati said dog bites should never be taken lightly. Rabies is a fatal viral disease that spreads through bites or scratches from dogs, cats or other animals. If anti-rabies injections are not given in time, the virus can spread rapidly and affect the brain, nervous system and heart, which can be fatal. Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of stray dogs According to 2019 data from the Union Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of stray dogs in the country — over 20.5 lakh. In Lucknow alone, surveys estimated between 75,000 and 95,000 stray dogs. Rules for Pet Dogs Rules for Stray Dogs (ABC Program)

stories.title: Human trafficking racket busted near Nepal border:Police rescue four girls being brought at night through dense jungle routes, two traffickers arrested
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Police have busted another gang involved in prostitution and human trafficking in Shravasti district. Four Nepali girls being brought into Uttar Pradesh through dense forest routes along the Nepal border were rescued by the police. Two traffickers were also arrested during the operation. Police said the girls were being brought from Nepal through forest routes late at night after being lured with false promises of work as dancers in orchestras. Acting on a tip-off, the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and local police carried out a joint operation and rescued the girls, who were being transported on two motorcycles. According to police, the girls were extremely frightened. On seeing the police, they panicked and began crying loudly. Female constables present with the rescue team counselled the girls and helped calm them down. It may be noted that Dainik Bhaskar had carried a special investigation report two days earlier exposing the trafficking of underage Nepali girls in the India–Nepal border areas. During the investigation, traffickers and agents had gone on camera explaining how girls are taken from small villages in Nepal and routed through Uttar Pradesh to major Indian cities and even Gulf countries. Following the report’s publication, border police, the SSB and local police had intensified surveillance and operations. Rescue operation in detail On January 31, 2026, Sub-Inspector Deepak Giri of Sirsiya police station was attending a border coordination meeting with the SSB along the India–Nepal border. During the meeting, an informer provided critical information that two Indian youths were bringing four Nepali girls into India via forest routes on motorcycles. Given the seriousness of the information, NGOs and the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) were immediately alerted, and a swift action plan was drawn up. Police teams set up a strategic blockade on the forest route ahead of Bhachkahi village in the Gujjar Gauri border area. Shortly afterwards, two motorcycles carrying two youths and four visibly distressed Nepali girls were spotted. The police intercepted the vehicles and apprehended the youths on the spot, successfully rescuing the four girls from falling into the trafficking network. During questioning, the arrested accused were identified as Hariram Yadav, son of Raksharam, and Ramroop, son of Ram Lotan—both residents of Babhani Kukurbhukva village under Sirsiya police station in Shravasti district. Preliminary investigations revealed that the accused were operating a local human trafficking network along the Nepal border. Police recovered two motorcycles, one Aadhaar card and two mobile phones from their possession. A case has been registered under serious sections related to human trafficking, and both accused have been sent to judicial custody. Police said the role of other members linked to the network is also being investigated. Orchestra lure, plan to send girls to different locations Interrogation revealed that the accused had shown the girls dreams of earning money by dancing in orchestras. In reality, they were preparing to send them to different locations, where the risk of exploitation was evident. SP: Vigilance increased along the border Superintendent of Police Rahul Bhati praised the operation and said the district follows a zero-tolerance policy against human trafficking. Surveillance has been stepped up in border areas, and such networks will be dismantled completely, he said.
