stories.title: Rinku Singh's Facebook account hacked, FIR lodged in Aligarh:Hackers changed ID, monetisation money also stolen
stories.summary: Indian cricketer Rinku Singh has fallen victim to cyber fraud after his official Facebook account was hacked. The hackers not only took control of the account but also diverted its monetisation earnings to their own account. A case has now been registered at the cybercrime police station following a complaint filed by Rinku’s brother, Sonu Singh. According to the complaint, Rinku was busy with international cricket commitments and preparations for the T20 World Cup, due to which he could not closely monitor his social media accounts. The issue came to light on February 4, when Rinku tried to log into his Facebook account and found that the password was no longer working. After repeated failed login attempts, Rinku informed his brother, who immediately approached the authorities. Following directions from the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), a formal case was registered and an investigation has begun. As investigations continue into the cyber fraud case, fans hope that Rinku’s account will be restored soon and justice will be served. How was the Facebook account hacked? Rinku Singh’s brother Sonu Singh, a resident of Ozone City Gold State, revealed that Rinku is currently in Mumbai after returning from a T20 World Cup warm-up match against South Africa. When Rinku attempted to access his Facebook account on February 4, he realised that the registered email ID had been changed. Despite not using the account, photos and videos were being uploaded, which raised suspicion. Earlier, the account was linked to the email ID (rinkukumar344.8.7), but it is now being operated using another email ID, (commercial.rinkukumar). This confirmed that the account had been taken over by hackers. The Facebook page has around 1.6 million followers and is monetised, generating significant income. Sonu stated that this income is now being transferred directly to the hackers’ account. Police action and account recovery efforts Cyber Crime Station Inspector Ramendra Shukla confirmed that a case has been registered against unknown persons. SSP Neeraj Kumar Jadaun said the cyber team has been instructed to trace the hackers, stop further financial loss, and recover the account as soon as possible. Police officials have assured the family that strict action will be taken and digital evidence is being examined. Engagement With MP Priya Saroj Apart from the cyber fraud case, Rinku Singh has also been in the news for his personal life. He got engaged to Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj on June 8 last year at a grand ring ceremony in Lucknow. The event was attended by several high-profile leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, and Jaya Bachchan. The wedding was initially planned for November 18 in Kashi but was postponed due to Rinku’s packed cricket schedule, including IPL and the T20 World Cup. A new date has not yet been finalised. A Journey from struggle to national stardom Rinku Singh’s rise to fame is a story of hard work and struggle. Coming from a modest background, his father worked as a gas cylinder deliveryman. Rinku and his brothers also helped deliver cylinders to support the family. Despite financial hardships, Rinku continued playing cricket with borrowed equipment and limited resources. His life changed after his iconic five sixes in IPL 2023 for Kolkata Knight Riders, which made him a household name.

stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, protests have erupted over the title of Manoj Bajpayee’s film Ghooskhor Pandat. An FIR has been registered against the film’s director in Lucknow. The complaint was filed by Inspector Vikram Singh at Hazratganj Kotwali on the Chief Minister’s instructions. Police say the film’s title and storyline incorrectly portray a particular caste and community, especially the Brahmin society, which could stir discontent and disturb law and order. Meanwhile, in Mathura, Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas president Dinesh Falahari Maharaj has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding an immediate ban on the film. He stated that the title unfairly portrays the community as ‘corrupt’, which is highly objectionable. Saints from Prayagraj have also voiced strong opposition. Shringerverpur Peethadheeshwar Jagadguru Ramanujacharya Swami Narayanacharya Shandilya Ji Maharaj said Bollywood exhibits a double standard, making films that repeatedly target specific groups, thereby creating societal divisions. Swami Brahmasram Maharaj, president of the Akhil Bharatiya Dandi Sanyasi Parishad, added that films like Ghooskhor Pandat harm Sanatan traditions and undermine mutual brotherhood. He too has demanded the film be banned immediately.

stories.title: Questions mount over deaths of three sisters:Father cites Korean influence, demands ban; investigation continues on multiple angles
stories.summary: On the night of 3 February, three sisters died after falling from a high-rise apartment in Ghaziabad. While an eight-page suicide note points to their deep immersion in Korean culture, several contradictions in the father’s statements and accounts from residents have raised serious questions. Initially, the father, Chetan Kumar, told police that his daughters died by suicide while completing the final task of a Korean online game. Later, he changed his version, saying the girls were addicted to Korean movies and social media reels. He claimed he had confiscated their mobile phones and warned them that if their behaviour did not improve, he would get them married. Chetan’s first wife, Sujata, told police that the girls had locked the room from inside and could not be saved. However, after this statement, both of Chetan’s wives locked themselves inside the flat and were unavailable for further questioning. Police are now examining Chetan’s statements, call detail records of both wives, bank transactions and forensic evidence from inside the flat. As the suicide narrative unfolds, multiple unanswered questions have emerged, which investigators are trying to resolve. To get closer to the truth behind the deaths of the three sisters, the Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to residents of Bharat City’s B-1 Tower, where the family lived in Flat No. 907. Several residents refused to speak on camera but raised significant doubts about the incident. Rajendra said - The girls were fighting, they might have been pushed Rajendra Sharma (75), a resident of the society, appeared disturbed by the deaths. He said that around 2 am on 3 February, his grandson was crying, so he stepped outside to calm him and walked around the ground floor. He said he heard shouting and sounds of children arguing. After some time, the noise stopped. About two to three minutes later, he heard the sound of someone falling. A few seconds later, he heard two more bodies hitting the ground in quick succession. He rushed to the spot and saw three girls lying on the ground, bleeding. By then, several neighbours had gathered. When asked about the sounds of argument, Rajendra said it felt like someone was trying to save someone else. He said it was possible that one girl slipped and the others fell while trying to save her. He also said it was possible they were pushed, as the distance between where the bodies landed was quite large. Why was the mother cursing her husband over the daughters' deaths? A woman from the society said that after news of the incident spread, residents rushed downstairs. She said she was going down in the lift when Chetan and his wife Sujata entered the lift as well. According to her, the couple were arguing, and Sujata was loudly abusing Chetan, repeatedly using foul language. Chetan remained silent. As soon as the lift doors opened, he rushed towards the spot where the bodies were lying. The woman said that even after seeing the bodies on the ground with blood scattered around, Sujata continued abusing her husband. She questioned how a mother could behave that way when the bodies of her three daughters were lying in front of her. People asked - The daughters died, then why is the father wearing a mask While talking to the residents of B-1 tower in the society, a person raised questions. He said - Chetan kept wearing a mask the whole time, someone whose 3 daughters have died is hiding his face. Think about it, when a child even gets a fever, parents become worried and don't even pay attention to what they're wearing. Even after such a big incident here, he remembered to wear a mask. The question is also why is he keeping himself separate from everyone? His face wasn't showing any signs of pain. Both mothers haven't appeared even 48 hours after death Neighbours said that after the girls fell from the balcony, both wives were seen briefly in the society, along with Chetan’s sister Tina. After that, the flat remained locked. The household includes Chetan, his two wives, his sister, a seven-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. When the Additional Police Commissioner tried to speak to both wives, they locked the door from inside. Not only the father, but both mothers also avoided facing people. On the evening of 5 February, some female relatives arrived at the flat and stood outside for 35 minutes. Chetan eventually opened the door, still wearing a mask, let them inside and immediately shut the door again without speaking to anyone. Why did the daughters only put their father's photo on the floor? A woman from a 10th-floor flat said the girls had cut out small photographs and pasted them on the floor of their room. She questioned why only the father’s photos were used and none of the mothers’. She said the three girls had two mothers, yet not a single photo of either mother was found. She said this raised questions about the girls’ emotional state and family dynamics. Why was 'sorry' written only for Papa in the diary? A resident from the 11th floor said that the diary recovered as a suicide note contained an apology addressed only to the father. He questioned why there was no mention of the mother, especially since daughters usually share their feelings with their mothers. He said the girls were very young, and something significant must have been troubling them for them to exclude their mothers entirely. Woman said - The real cause of children's death should come to light Another woman resident, Isha Tyagi, said people should not jump to conclusions about Korean culture, mobile addiction or games. She said the real cause of death must come out. She said what was most shocking was that three children died together. She said it might be understandable if one child was disturbed, but three siblings dying together pointed to something far more serious. Father says - Korean videos should be banned in India The mystery surrounding the suicide of the three sisters continues to deepen. Attempts were made to speak to the girls’ father, but he refused to open the door and responded only from behind the mesh gate. The father said the children had created Korean-style identities and had even changed their names. He demanded that the government ban Korean dramas and videos, claiming such content is making children addicted. “My three children are gone. My life is gone,” he said, adding that such content should be stopped so that no other child loses their life. It may be noted that three minor sisters — Nishika (16), Prachi (14) and Pakhi (12) — died by suicide after jumping from the balcony around 2 am on 3 February. In their eight-page suicide note, the girls wrote, “Sorry Papa, I am really sorry.” Their last rites were performed in Delhi on 5 February. After the cremation, the father, Chetan, returned to his flat in Ghaziabad. Family has been living in rented flat for three years Chetan Kumar does online share trading. He has been living in a rented flat in Bharat Society for the past 3 years with his 2 wives Sujata and Hina and 5 children. Among the girls who committed suicide, Nishika was the daughter of Chetan's first wife Sujata, while Prachi and Pakhi were daughters of second wife Hina. When Chetan's first wife Sujata could not conceive for many years, he married Sujata's sister Hina (his sister-in-law). Just a few months after this, Sujata gave birth to Nishika. Second wife Hina gave birth to Prachi, Pakhi and another daughter. Later, the first wife had a son Lavish (7), who is mentally challenged and cannot speak. Police investigation continues DCP Says - Investigating All Angles DCP Trans Hindon Nimish Patil - All angles are being examined. The family’s silence, the mothers not coming forward and several links in the sequence of events are under investigation. Statements are being recorded, and new facts are likely to emerge soon ..

stories.title: UGC move worsens BJP’s troubles in UP:BJP and RSS confront renewed caste equations, Hindu vote bank splits, losses possible in 2027 polls
stories.summary: To mobilise the Hindu vote bank in favour of the BJP, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath gave the slogan, “If we remain divided, we will be cut down; if we stay united, we will remain safe.” Prime Minister Narendra Modi later echoed this sentiment by saying, “If we stay united, we will remain righteous.” For the last one-and-a-half years, the BJP had been trying to unite voters on religious lines instead of caste. However, the new rules issued by the University Grants Commission (UGC) have dealt a serious blow to this strategy. As a result, the Hindu vote bank has once again started breaking up along caste lines. Ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, feedback coming in from across Uttar Pradesh has increased BJP’s worries. This is why the state BJP leadership is now waiting for a decision and clear strategy from the Centre, hoping it may help limit the damage. Found counter to PDA, but now a new challenge In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party’s PDA (Backward Classes–Dalits–Minorities) slogan proved more effective than BJP’s nationalism and Hindutva pitch. BJP-led NDA saw its tally fall sharply from 66 seats to 36. The Samajwadi Party won 37 seats, while Congress secured 6, taking the INDIA alliance’s total to 43. After the results, political analysts widely agreed that SP’s caste-based mobilisation outperformed BJP and RSS’s religion-centric strategy, showing that caste politics had a greater electoral impact than the Hindutva narrative. Taking lessons from the Lok Sabha setback, BJP and RSS began working on a counter to SP’s PDA formula. During high-level discussions, it emerged that Hindus needed to be united again beyond caste divisions. Around the same time, incidents of attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh were reported. Referring to these incidents, CM Yogi Adityanath gave the slogan, If we remain divided, we will be cut down; if we stay united, we will remain safe to unite Hindus across the country and the state. RSS backing and Modi’s endorsement RSS fully backed Yogi’s slogan. In a meeting held in Mathura, the RSS also accepted that “If we remain divided, we will be cut down; if we stay united, we will remain safe” should be promoted. After this, Prime Minister Narendra Modi strengthened the message further by saying, “If we stay united, we will remain righteous.” BJP’s Hindutva-based politics appeared to work. By consolidating the Hindu vote bank, the party won by-elections in both 2024 and 2025. BJP, RSS and the organisation had been consistently working for nearly one-and-a-half years to unite Hindus on religious lines rather than caste, specifically to counter SP’s PDA narrative. However, in January 2026, the new UGC rules caused such disruption that upper-caste versus backward-Dalit politics resurfaced not only in Uttar Pradesh but across the country. Opposition came from upper-caste youth, government officers, women, senior citizens, salaried professionals and intellectuals, who openly protested against the rules. The issue reached the Supreme Court, which has currently stayed the implementation of the rules. BJP angered its core voters Political analysts point out that Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Kayasthas and Bhumihars form BJP’s core voter base. The very foundation of the BJP rests on the political support of these communities. By introducing the new UGC rules, the central government has ended up angering its own core voters. Analysts say that no political party in the country willingly takes the risk of upsetting its core support base. In BJP’s history, this is the first time that party workers and office-bearers resigned in protest against a policy decision. In several places, BJP flags were even removed from homes and thrown away. Distances increased between castes Political analysts say that even though the Supreme Court has stayed the UGC rules, they have already created visible gaps between upper castes, backward classes and Dalits. These divisions are now being seen not only among students but also among teachers in colleges and universities. On Wednesday, clashes broke out between two groups of students over the UGC rules at Banaras Hindu University and Allahabad University. On social media, both sides continue to accuse each other. Dalit and backward-class youth are angry with upper-caste intellectuals opposing the UGC rules. At the same time, upper-caste youth are openly expressing anger against Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and several BJP leaders. UGC has created division in society Senior journalist and political analyst Ramdatt Tripathi says the UGC rules have led to social fragmentation. He says the situation resembles the period when the Mandal Commission recommendations were implemented. According to him, SC/ST and OBC communities believe the rules were in their favour and should have been implemented. Upper-caste communities, however, feel the rules were against them. Tripathi adds that the central government should have spoken to people, consulted stakeholders and explained why the rules were necessary before implementing them. Although the Supreme Court has stayed the rules, he says the damage has already been done, and Dalit, backward and upper-caste communities are all turning against BJP over the issue. RSS worried during its centenary year RSS is organising Hindu conferences across the country during its centenary year to unite Hindus. In such a situation, the UGC rules have become a major cause of concern for the organisation. An RSS office-bearer said the impact of this division is now visible even at the village level. People from both sections are unhappy, and if the divide continues, it will also affect RSS programmes. UGC splits Hindu vote bank Senior journalist Sunita Aron says the UGC issue has split the Hindu vote bank. She refers to BJP’s long-held political assumption: “Out of 100, 60 are ours; the rest are divided, and even in that division, we gain.” She says PM Modi and CM Yogi tried to consolidate Hindu voters through projects like the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, the Mahakal Corridor and other religious-spiritual initiatives. However, the UGC rules have now caused a clear split in that vote base. What BJP is doing for damage control Amid nationwide protests and Supreme Court intervention over the UGC issue, a meeting was held on Wednesday at the Delhi residence of Raipur MP Brijmohan Agrawal to discuss future strategy. The meeting included two Union ministers involved in preparing the UGC committee report and around 15 MPs. MP Brijmohan Agrawal said all members were trying to resolve the issue in line with BJP and PM Modi’s Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas approach. Union Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, senior BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad, New Delhi MP Bansuri Swaraj, Hoshangabad MP Darshan Chaudhary, Rajya Sabha MP Dr Bhim Singh, MP Abhijit Bandopadhyay and several other leaders participated and shared their views. Now waiting for the Center's decision Political observers say the Uttar Pradesh BJP is now waiting for a decision from the Centre on the UGC issue. The central government and BJP’s national leadership will decide how to address the fragmentation in the vote bank, and the state unit will follow the same line.

stories.title: Details of family dispute emerge in Ghaziabad triple suicide case:Father had 3 wives, sister-in-law also lived together, suicide note deepens mystery
stories.summary: Fresh details have emerged in the case of three sisters who died by suicide after jumping from ninth-floor of an apartment building in Ghaziabad on the night of February 3. While several aspects related to the children’s father have come to light during the investigation, the mother has not yet given a formal statement to the police, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the incident. Witnesses said that when the girls fell from the building, their mother ran downstairs screaming, crying loudly, abusing family members and covering the girls’ bloodstained bodies with her clothes. However, once the police took the bodies into custody and sent them to the mortuary, the mother was taken away separately. Since then, no family member has come forward to speak publicly. They spoke to some people connected to the family. Let's understand... Case linked to domestic conflict, not just financial stress While the deaths have been linked to financial hardship, people close to the family say the situation was worsened by daily domestic disputes. Frequent arguments inside the home allegedly left the children neglected and emotionally isolated. The Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to neighbours and people familiar with the family to understand the internal conflicts that may have led to the tragedy. Father married two sisters, third wife from Muslim community The family lived in Flat No. 907, B-1 Tower, in Bharat City Society, located in the Tila Mor area, about 20 km from Ghaziabad district headquarters. The society has over 1,000 flats. The father, Chetan, lived in the flat with three wives. Two of them—Sujata and Heena—are real sisters, while the third wife belongs to the Muslim community. Another sister of Sujata and Heena would also stay at the flat occasionally. In total, five children lived in the apartment. At around 2 am on February 4, three girls fell from the ninth floor and died on the spot. Since then, the family has kept the flat locked. Neighbours report frequent arguments before incident Local women told reporters that loud arguments and verbal abuse were heard from the flat shortly before the incident. A society resident, Nisha Chaturvedi, said the girls’ mother rushed downstairs crying after the fall, shouting that she would expose everything. She alleged that while the mother was distraught, the father appeared calm and unaffected. Several residents questioned how all three girls could take such a step together. They also pointed out that the children did not attend school, despite nearby government schools being available. Nisha Chaturvedi, also from the society, says that when the girls fell, their mother ran downstairs. She was screaming loudly. She was saying that she would tell everyone. She was also swearing. She was taking off her clothes and putting them over the children. She took off her sweater and put it on them, then put her shawl over them. She was crying a lot. But her husband did not seem restless or troubled. Family lived in isolation Neighbours said the family rarely interacted with others. Rajiv Chauhan, who lives in Flat No. 904 on the same floor, said he had never spoken to them and had only seen the children once or twice in the lift. Other residents, speaking off-camera, described the household as deeply troubled, marked by constant conflict. They said the children appeared withdrawn and neglected. Mothers remain silent, family refuses to speak After the incident, four women were seen leaving the flat with a male relative who refused to speak. Later, it was revealed that Sujata and Heena had come from Seelampur, Delhi, after receiving news of their daughters’ deaths. A woman familiar with the family said both mothers were inconsolable and unable to speak. Sujata’s mother was also present and trying to comfort them. Family background and children Sujata is the eldest of nine sisters. After she failed to conceive for three years, the family arranged Chetan’s marriage with her younger sister Heena. Heena gave birth to Nishika and Prachi, while Sujata later gave birth to Cindy and a seven-year-old differently abled son who cannot speak or hear. Contrary to earlier reports, locals clarified that the third wife was not the sister-in-law, but a Muslim woman who also has a four-year-old daughter. However, the sister-in-law did stay with the family occasionally. Position of bodies raises suspicion The manner in which the bodies were found has raised serious questions. After falling from the ninth floor: Residents questioned how someone jumping from that height could land so close to the building wall, deepening suspicion around the incident. Suicide note suggests abuse Police recovered a suicide note in which the word “I” was used instead of “we”, suggesting it may have been written by only one of the girls. One line in the note reads: “It is better to die than to be beaten.” This has strengthened suspicions that the children may have faced physical abuse at home. Police continue to investigate all angles in the case.

stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Union government for denying facts surrounding former Army chief General MM Naravane’s memoir. Kharge accused the government of evading questions on national security and China, leading to an Opposition walkout from Rajya Sabha.

stories.title: Dubai, Sharjah to see rain as temperatures hold at 24°C; authorities issue advisory
stories.summary: Dubai and UAE brace for intermittent light rain and cloudy skies, particularly in the early morning hours. Coastal areas may experience fog, impacting visibility. While northern regions anticipate more showers, Dubai's rainfall is expected to be brief. This unstable weather, influenced by pressure shifts, is typical for the winter transition.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia revokes licences of 74 private schools over safety and regulatory violations
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Education has revoked the operating licenses of 74 private schools due to repeated regulatory violations, including expired licenses and lack of safety certifications. This decisive action aims to protect student safety and uphold educational standards across the Kingdom.

stories.title: 'People reject you & you use judicial platform to get popularity': SC raps Prashant Kishor’s Jan Suraaj over Bihar polls plea
'Epitome of women empowerment': PM Modi welcomes students to 'Pariksha Pe Charcha' with 'Gamosa' — Watch
Pariksha Pe Charcha 2026: PM Modi urges students to focus on skills, stress-free learning—top quotes
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi engaged with students nationwide in the 9th Pariksha Pe Charcha, offering guidance on exams, personal growth, and nation-building. He emphasized the importance of dreams, action, balance in life, and the equal significance of life and professional skills, urging students to avoid treating education as a burden and focus on holistic development.

stories.title: Dubai traffic alert today: Major road closures announced for UAE Tour Women 2026
stories.summary: Dubai gears up to host the UAE Tour Women 2026's second stage this Friday, February 6. Cyclists will traverse iconic city routes, leading to brief, rolling road closures for 10-15 minutes. Motorists are advised to plan ahead for temporary disruptions as the emirate showcases its commitment to women's cycling and recreational sports.

stories.title: $16 billion funding freeze: Trump wanted NY airport, station named after him, says report
Naravane memoir row: Kiren Rijiju cites book to target Nehru, counter Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: A political row erupted in Parliament over Rahul Gandhi quoting former Army Chief General MM Naravane's memoir. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju defended the government's decision to keep the Henderson Brooks-Bhagat report on the 1962 war classified. He stated the report is a sensitive defence document and should not be used for political purposes.

stories.title: AI, fake me a prescription
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence is facilitating the procurement of restricted drugs, including antibiotics and addictive medications, through AI-generated prescriptions. Investigations revealed that fake prescriptions, even with hospital logos, can be used to obtain medicines from online and offline pharmacies, raising significant patient safety and drug misuse concerns. Experts warn of escalating antimicrobial resistance and addiction risks due to weak verification.

stories.title: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey proposes to set-up library on ‘misdeeds’ of Nehru-Gandhi family
stories.summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey announced plans to establish a library documenting alleged "misdeeds, corruption and policy failures" of the Nehru-Gandhi family. He appealed for contributions of books and documents, aiming to create a consolidated resource for students and researchers on the Congress party's first family.

stories.title: UAE: Sheikh Hamdan inaugurates driverless RT6 taxi operations in Dubai
stories.summary: Dubai has officially begun testing fully autonomous RT6 taxis on public roads, a significant stride in integrating AI into its transport system. Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum experienced a ride, showcasing the technology's readiness. This paves the way for a public launch in early 2026, with plans for over 1,000 vehicles.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia: Ministry of Hajj and Umrah to begin issuing Hajj 2026 visas from Sunday
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has launched visa processing for the 2026 Hajj season, nearly four months ahead of schedule. This proactive measure, part of Vision 2030, aims to enhance service readiness, improve pilgrim comfort, and streamline logistics. Contracts for holy site services and Makkah accommodations are finalized, with significant pilgrim registration already underway, ensuring a more organized pilgrimage.

stories.title: Savannah Guthrie’s missing mother: Blood on porch, ransom notes surface; family pleads for answers in new video
stories.summary: An 84-year-old woman, Nancy Guthrie, mother of "Today" show host Savannah Guthrie, remains missing after her suspected abduction from her Tucson home. Investigators are treating ransom notes demanding millions in bitcoin as credible, with deadlines set for Thursday and Monday. The family has pleaded for direct contact to confirm her well-being.

stories.title: How the Green River managed to cut straight through the already existing Uinta Mountains; scientists are surprised to know
Can’t cite funds crunch to stop DA payment: SC to West Bengal govt
stories.summary: SC rejected Bengal govt’s defence it lacked funds and said it is not open for the State to shirk its responsibility of paying DA on account of financial difficulty, given that it is an obligation arising out of a statute of its own creation. SC said the least that is expected of a State in a democracy is that it honours its obligations and commitments arising from a legislation or judicial decisions, for such obligations are not discretionary.

stories.title: Pawar family backs Sunetra as NCP chief
stories.summary: Possibility of a re-unification grew stronger after Pawar Senior took the lead to minimise tension within the family when he went to meet Sunetra and her sons at their Baramati residence for the second consecutive day on Thursday. Some senior NCP members, including Patel and state chief Sunil Tatkare, have refuted Sharad Pawar’s claim that his nephew had initiated steps for NCP’s merger.

stories.title: India may raise Zakir Naik issue again during PM’s Malaysia visit
stories.summary: India and Malaysia have an extradition treaty, but the case, as Malaysia maintains, will be resolved based on judicial consideration. The official said that Modi and his counterpart Anwar Ibrahim will review progress under the India-Malaysia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, especially in priority areas of cooperation such as trade, investments, defence, security, semiconductors, digital technologies, renewable energy, education, healthcare, and people-to-people exchanges.

stories.title: Migration ban on medics invalid, Delhi HC asks NMC to frame policy
At 57.4k, deaths on NHs down by 11% in 2025: Govt
Ensure compliance with all poll laws: EC to observers
stories.summary: Addressing central observers at India International Institute of Democracy and Electoral Management (IIIDEM) here, chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar said they had been picked by EC to act as its beacons for the assembly polls in Assam, Kerala, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. Polls in the four states and Puducherry are likely to be held in April-May. A total of 1,444 observers are to be briefed in three batches on Thursday and Friday.

stories.title: In 10 years, trial courts awarded death to 1,310, high courts upheld 106
India’s agricultural interests fully secure under US deal: Chouhan
stories.summary: Underlining that India’s staple grains, fruits, major crops, millets and dairy products remain completely secure and face no threat whatsoever, Chouhan emphasised that the interests of small and large farmers alike have been fully protected and that the agreement will create fresh opportunities rather than risks for Indian agriculture. He said that reduced tariffs will directly benefit India’s rice, spices and textile exports, and that growth in textile exports will help millions of cotton-growing farmers.

stories.title: Railways sees FY27 passenger, freight earnings rise, but FY26 falls short of Budget target
stories.summary: In the freight segment, the ministry has estimated earning of around Rs 1.88 lakh crore in FY 27, same that osf BE of FY26 and 6% higher than the RE of current fiscal year. Data also show that railways is likely to end up generating around Rs 1.78 lakh crore by March, around 5.5% less than the target it had set for the current year.

stories.title: Teacher who reached out to never-been-to-school kids, drew wall murals to educate them honoured with $1m global prize
stories.summary: Global Teacher Prize 2026 was presented at World Governments Summit in Dubai, an annual gathering of leaders and policymakers. Now in its tenth year, the prize — an initiative of Varkey Foundation along with Unesco — honours teachers whose work reshaped learning outcomes and communities. Nagi, who has developed pedagogy around art, began her work in the slums of Mumbai about a decade ago.

stories.title: CPWD bought 405 air purifiers in 4 years, for babus & courts
stories.summary: In a written reply, housing and urban affairs ministry said during 2023–24 and 2024–25, CPWD procured 300 air purifiers. “The devices were issued to offices, chambers, VVIP lounges, dining halls of judges and registrar of SC, courtrooms, ministers, Constitution Club of India, LS/RS secretariats in Parliament complex and various offices of ministries, departments at Nirman Bhavan, Sewa Bhavan, Vigyan Bhavan, and CPWD offices at Jodhpur and Varanasi,” it said.

stories.title: Fearing ‘unpleasant act’ by oppn, asked PM to skip Lok Sabha: Birla
stories.summary: “Had such an unpleasant act happened, then its sight would have torn the country’s democratic traditions to shreds,” Om Birla said amid protests from opposition MPs. PM Modi’s scheduled reply to the Motion of Thanks on the President’s address was called off at last minute on Wednesday due to intense protest from opposition MPs.

stories.title: Autonomy pact inked for 6 Nagaland districts
stories.summary: As part of the arrangement, there will be devolution of powers relating to 46 subjects to FNTA, which will cover the districts of Tuensang, Mon, Kiphire, Longleng, Noklak and Shamator. The autonomy and greater say will address the long-standing grievances of ENPO over lack of equitable development in eastern Nagaland districts.

stories.title: NCLT recalls order awarding Alchemist to ‘sister concern’
stories.summary: The withdrawal of the corporate resolution order by NCLT, a rare occurrence, happened after Enforcement Directorate approached the Delhi bench with evidence of money laundering by the group and how the promoters had allegedly created a front entity with “proceeds of crime”, making it a financial creditor with 97% voting rights to grab the firm under insolvency proceedings.

stories.title: Unlike in 3 other opposition states, West Bengal sees governor-govt cordiality
stories.summary: West Bengal governor CV Ananda Bose read out portions of the address highlighting law and order, including references to Kolkata being among the safest cities in the country. In a rare display of cordiality, he was even seen briefly holding hands and speaking with CM Mamata Banerjee after his address, prompting BJP legislators to sarcastically comment “well done”, as he exited the House.

stories.title: Treat Chinese manjha deaths as murder, CM Yogi orders officials
stories.summary: Asked how the directive will be implemented, additional chief secretary (home) Sanjay Prasad said, “We are working on a legal and procedural framework to ensure any death caused due to the use of banned Chinese manjha is treated as a case of murder. Clear instructions will be issued to the police so that strict action can be taken against all those involved in its sale, supply or use.”

stories.title: Manipur erupts over Nemcha Kipgen as new deputy CM
stories.summary: ​​The influential Kuki Zo Council declared a social boycott of any legislator from the community joining CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh’s govt. Protesters burned tyres and blocked roads in Kangpokpi district, and at least one group called for a shutdown in the hills. In Kangpokpi, roads littered with burning tyres signalled a return to unrest after a period of relative calm across the hills.

stories.title: Brooklyn Beckham removes ‘Dad’ arm tattoo dedicated to David Beckham amid public fallout
stories.summary: Brooklyn Beckham has visibly escalated his estrangement from his family by removing tattoos honoring his parents, covering “Dad” on his arm and replacing his “mama’s boy” chest tattoo with a floral design. The changes, alongside his public statements about family tensions, mark a clear break from tradition, making his body art a striking symbol of his rift with Victoria and David Beckham.

stories.title: Critical minerals cooperation with US advancing rapidly: Jaishankar
stories.summary: According to the MEA, Jaishankar, in the meeting, highlighted the challenges of excessive concentration and the importance of de-risking supply, and also spoke about structured international cooperation. Jaishankar said on X that the deal opens up a new phase in India-US bilateral ties, with vast possibilities for the relationship, signalling renewed high-level engagements in the next few months.

stories.title: Didi’s poll sop: Stipend for jobless youth, hike in payout to women
stories.summary: Finance minister Chandrima Bhattacharya on Thursday had some cheer for state govt employees too, budgeting for a 4% hike in DA. Govt rechristened its Karmashree scheme as “Mahatma Shree” and hiked the minimum number of workdays from 75 to 100 in what is being seen as a nod to Trinamool Congress’s opposition to the Centre’s decision to replace MGNREGA.

stories.title: Rs 3,200 crore stuck in Northeast projects; Assam tops unpaid list
stories.summary: State-wise figures show Assam topping the list with Rs 1,012.87 crore pending across 35 projects, followed by Manipur (Rs 441.38 crore), Nagaland (Rs 406.09 crore) and Arunachal Pradesh (Rs 395.37 crore). Other states with large unpaid amounts include Tripura (Rs 308.71 crore), Mizoram (Rs 275.81 crore), Meghalaya (Rs 258.05 crore) and Sikkim (Rs 107.90 crore).

stories.title: Open to exploring oil supplies from Venezuela: Govt
stories.summary: “Consistent with India’s approach to energy security, India remains open to exploring the commercial merits of any new crude supply options, including from Venezuela,” said the official. On India’s energy sourcing, the official recalled that govt had stated publicly on several occasions that ensuring the energy security of 1.4 billion Indians was the supreme priority of govt.

stories.title: In Rajya Sabha, Kharge refers to LS row, draws BJP fire
stories.summary: Kharge’s reference to LS proceedings drew a sharp response from BJP, with Leader of the House in RS JP Nadda mocking Rahul as “abodh balak (ignorant child)” and reminding Kharge that events of one House cannot be debated in another. Nadda asked Kharge not to let Congress become “hostage” to Rahul and said arrogance and ignorance should not dictate actions.

stories.title: Police can’t arrest an accused simply to ask questions: Supreme Court
stories.summary: Enumerating various sections of the newly enacted Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and N K Singh said a notice under Section 35(3) of the law to an accused or any individual concerned, qua offences punishable with imprisonment of up to 7 years, is the rule.

stories.title: Deals with EU, US good sign for world stability: PM Modi in Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: PM Modi’s remarks in Rajya Sabha, during the debate on the motion of thanks on the President’s address, came even as the treaty with the US is yet to be formally signed. It’s being seen as an indication that the two sides may have resolved their differences. The formal announcement of the deal is likely next week.

stories.title: 'Protecting infiltrators': PM Modi slams TMC; flays Congress for 'harbouring hatred'
IndiGo’s December disruption stranded 16.2 lakh domestic flyers: DGCA
stories.summary: The directorate’s monthly traffic data for Dec 2025 says 16.2 lakh domestic flyers were stranded at airports across the country due to the non-availability of either IndiGo aircraft or their crew members. The number of people affected due to total cancellation of flights was 9.8 lakh, while those stranded at the airports due to delays beyond two hours were 6.4 lakh.

stories.title: 5 LCA Mk1A fighter jets fully ready for delivery to IAF: HAL
stories.summary: HAL said that “an additional nine aircraft have already been built and flown. Upon receipt of engines from General Electric (US company), these aircraft will be made ready for delivery”. “All design and development issues identified are being addressed in an expedited manner. HAL is in active discussions with IAF to deliver the aircraft at the earliest,” it said in a statement.

stories.title: Married woman can’t claim rape on false marriage promise: Supreme Court
stories.summary: A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan said in such cases, a woman was not eligible to get married due to the subsistence of her marriage and she could not invoke the ground of false promise of marriage. It passed the order while quashing criminal proceedings against a lawyer on a complaint filed by a woman advocate alleging that he had raped her on the false promise of marriage.

stories.title: KSI admits he was “washed” on YouTube after struggling to hit one million views
stories.summary: British creator KSI openly admitted to a difficult period on YouTube in mid-2025, where his videos struggled to reach one million views, leading him to feel "fallen off." Despite external successes, he recommitted to the platform, and his main channel has since seen view counts surpass the one million mark, indicating a gradual comeback.

stories.title: 'To our Indian community, you are home in Frisco': Major outrage over targeting of Indians at Frisco City Council meeting
TheBurntPeanut’s rapid Twitch rise sparks viewbotting accusations on social media
stories.summary: Twitch streamer TheBurntPeanut is facing accusations of viewbotting following a rapid surge in viewership, with some streams attracting tens of thousands of viewers. Critics point to unusual viewership patterns and low chat activity as evidence, while supporters attribute the growth to successful social media content. The debate continues as no official statements have been made.

stories.title: NATO wargame shows Russia conquers the Baltics in days as US holds back and Europe hesitates
stories.summary: A German-led wargame suggests Russia could secure key objectives in the Baltics within days by exploiting alliance hesitation and political ambiguity. A simulated incursion into southern Lithuania showed Nato members delaying military responses, allowing Moscow to establish control without major escalation. The exercise highlights how decision-making dynamics and expectations, rather than force alone, could shape outcomes in a future crisis.

stories.title: Don't lecture: Heated exchange between Polish PM, US ambassador over Trump Nobel row
YouTube reveals $60 billion revenue in 2025, surpassing Netflix for the first time
stories.summary: YouTube has officially revealed its impressive financial performance, generating over $60 billion in revenue for 2025 through advertising and paid subscriptions. This significant figure surpasses Netflix and highlights YouTube's evolution into a dominant global media powerhouse. The platform's growth is fueled by increasing viewer engagement and a strong performance from its subscription services.

stories.title: 'When your studies are over...': Expert advises how to answer officer's trick question for US student visa interview
Pir Panjal row roils J&K assembly as BJP MLA refuses apology
stories.summary: The row comes weeks after PDP president Mehbooba Mufti pitched for a separate administrative division comprising Rajouri and Poonch in Pir Panjal along with Chenab valley districts, citing remoteness, hilly terrain and lack of infrastructure — a demand BJP opposed. The region refers to the mountainous belt along the Pir Panjal range south of Kashmir valley and close to the LoC.

stories.title: Govt questions Sixth Schedule limits, statehood fiscal burden at Ladakh talks
stories.summary: Govt also sought clarity on the financial burden of granting Ladakh full statehood with a legislature, including salaries, provident fund liabilities and other expenditures for about 19,000 employees. Running a state or a Union territory with a legislature involves managing deficits and long-term fiscal responsibility, prompting the panel to press Ladakhi activists for detailed projections, the sources said.

stories.title: IED found in Rajouri; balloon with PIA marking seized in Udhampur
‘J&K reported 2 lakh dog bites cases in past 2 years’
Passage of motion of thanks in LS without PM’s reply constitutes procedural irregularities: Cong MP
Congress MP Tankha writes to Shah seeking release of climate activist Wangchuk
Centre, Nagaland govt and ENPO sign agreement to create Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority
'Deeply disappointing': Cops charged in Canada for working with extortion gang, drug traffickers; they leaked personal information to criminals
Hammam mein sab…: Why Donald Trump remains untouched by the Epstein files (so far)
stories.summary: Trump appears in the Epstein files in a strangely spectral way. His name is everywhere, but his voice is nowhere. He shows up in third-party emails, in interview notes, in calendars, in contact lists, and in messages where other people discuss him as a destination, a favour, or a point of access.

stories.title: Focused policy and transparent decision-making: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta on BJP Govt's nearly one year in office
stories.summary: the Delhi CM asserted that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led administration prioritised policy decisions and accountability after forming government on February 20, 2025.

stories.title: ‘Importing radical Islam will destroy America’: Texas congressman Brandon Gill warns of ‘consequences like Europe’
stories.summary: Texas lawmaker Brandon Gill's viral speech linking immigration to radical Islam and citing Europe's challenges sparked fierce online debate. He warned of security and social threats, drawing parallels to European integration issues. Supporters lauded his stance on national security, while critics accused him of conflating Islam with extremism and ignoring Muslim history in America.

stories.title: 'Happy to eat your share of samosas': MAGA influencer slams pastor for speaking up for Indians
Violence in Manipur: Police, mob clash during protests against deputy CM appointment
stories.summary: Protests erupted in Manipur's Churachandpur district following MLA Nemcha Kipgen's appointment as deputy chief minister, leading to clashes. Demonstrators set fire to discarded materials and hurled stones at security forces who responded with a baton charge. Two individuals sustained minor injuries, and additional forces have been deployed to manage the tense situation.

stories.title: ‘Bengal ki nirmam sarkar, insult to people of Assam’: Poll-bound states find special mention in PM Modi’s Rajya Sabha speech
PM Modi’s Malaysia visit to strengthen strategic partnership — what to watch for
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Malaysia on February 7-8 to strengthen ties and expand cooperation under a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. He will hold bilateral talks with PM Anwar Ibrahim, review key sectors like trade and defense, and address the Indian community. The visit aims to deepen engagement with the ASEAN region and boost business ties.

stories.title: "Pollution is a legacy problem resulting from negligence of previous govts": Rekha Gupta
stories.summary: "Pollution is a legacy problem resulting from the negligence of previous governments. If we look at pollution only from the perspective that the air should be clean, we will not get results. You have to work on dust, air and water together, with a holistic vision," she said.

stories.title: 'Scared of truth, sought refuge in lies': Rahul Gandhi reacts to PM Modi's RS speech
Protego: How JK Rowling denied entry to Jeffrey Epstein
stories.summary: Jeffrey Epstein was denied entry to the 2018 Broadway premiere of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, despite intermediaries securing tickets. Justice Department files reveal he was never on the official guest list and event staff turned him away. JK Rowling, who had no contact with Epstein, was falsely accused of inviting him.

stories.title: Epstein Files: New email shows Ghislaine Maxwell explains controversial photo of Prince Andrew and Virginia Giuffre
stories.summary: Newly released US justice records reveal a 2015 draft email in which Ghislaine Maxwell set out her account of the disputed photograph linking Prince Andrew and Virginia Giuffre. The document, exchanged with Jeffrey Epstein as allegations intensified, contradicts earlier denials, fuels scrutiny of Andrew’s account, and has been seized on by Giuffre’s family as vindication after years of dispute.

stories.title: 'They stole surname of Mahatma Gandhi': PM Modi mocks Gandhis, takes failed 'start-up' jab at Rahul
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi sharply criticised the Congress and the Gandhi family in the Rajya Sabha, accusing them of being "habitual thieves" and alleging they stole Mahatma Gandhi's surname. He also targeted Rahul Gandhi, calling him "Yuvraj" and criticizing his "traitor" remark against a Sikh MP, which he deemed an insult to Sikhs and the community's sacrifices.

stories.title: Laura Loomer praises Trump’s ‘huge heart’ amid Savannah Guthrie’s mother’s disappearance
Tamil Nadu elections: How BJP plans to do a Bihar in state and will it be enough?
stories.summary: The BJP is attempting to replicate its Bihar electoral strategy in Tamil Nadu by consolidating opposition forces and forming a broad social alliance across major caste segments. Aiming to counter the DMK, the party is forging alliances with former partners and breakaway factions, including the AIADMK and PMK, to build a wider NDA for the upcoming assembly elections.

stories.title: 'Modi teri kabr khudegi': PM Modi accuses opposition of masking hate behind 'Mohabbat ki dukaan'
‘Conflict nearing end’: Centre, Nagaland and ENPO sign Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority agreement — what it means
stories.summary: The Central government, Nagaland government, and ENPO have signed an agreement to establish the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority (FNTA) to address the demands of Eastern Nagaland. Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated the MHA will fund the new body and ensure development in the region, marking progress towards peace and development in the Northeast.

stories.title: ‘Not American enough’: Vivek Ramaswamy faces backlash over daughter’s 'Hindu' name Savithri
stories.summary: Ohio Republican Vivek Ramaswamy faced online criticism for his daughter Savithri's name, deemed 'un-American' by some. The Sanskrit name, rooted in Hindu tradition, sparked debate on cultural identity and assimilation. Supporters defended the choice, highlighting America's diverse naming heritage, while detractors expressed xenophobic sentiments. The incident underscores ongoing tensions in American identity politics.

stories.title: CM Rekha Gupta urges plastic industry to enhance recycling to make Delhi cleaner, greener
'Congress hates Sikhs': PM Modi slams Rahul Gandhi's 'traitor' remark
'I eat 2kg of gaalis daily': In light moment during RS speech, PM Modi reveals 'health secret'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered a strong speech in Rajya Sabha criticising the Congress for decades of misgovernance and alleged deep hatred towards him. Modi also targeted Rahul Gandhi's recent comments, calling them an insult to Sikhs. The Prime Minister stated that much of the NDA's work involves correcting past mistakes.

stories.title: Explained: Why Epstein emails have become a ticking time bomb for Keir Starmer
stories.summary: The immediate spark was Starmer’s decision to publicly apologise to Epstein’s victims for appointing Peter Mandelson as Britain’s ambassador to the United States. The apology was unprecedented. A sitting prime minister saying sorry not for something he personally did, but for something he authorised, knowing it would reopen trauma for victims of one of the most notorious abusers of modern times.

stories.title: Kuwait announces shorter working hours for government employees during Ramadan 2026
stories.summary: Kuwaiti government employees will now work a shorter four-and-a-half-hour day during Ramadan, with flexible start times between 8:30 am and 10:30 am. This new framework, approved by the Civil Service Commission, aims to balance public service continuity with employee well-being during the fasting month. The flexible arrangement will be an annual practice.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Modi attacks opposition in Rajya Sabha as MPs stage walkout; LS Speaker says he asked PM to skip House & more
Why science says ghosts do not exist: The real reasons behind a most human belief
'Former H-1B': Indian-American community celebrates Balaji Krishnamoorthy becoming Uber CFO amid ongoing visa row
'Kharge can sit and shout slogans': PM Modi's dig at opposition leaders protesting in Rajya Sabha
Infiltrators, Congress and a jibe at Kharge: Top quotes from PM Modi's reply to motion of thanks in Rajya Sabha
Swatting During Brighton IRL Stream: Police detain Tubbo’s group after hoax call; streamer vows caution
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Tubbo revealed he was swatted during a live IRL pub crawl stream in Brighton after a false report claimed his friend was carrying a knife and drugs. Police detained and handcuffed the friend before confirming the call was a hoax. Tubbo called it a “seriously unfunny prank” and warned about the real dangers of swatting.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Don Zimmer: "What you lack in talent can be made up with desire, hustle and giving 110% all the time."
stories.summary: Don Zimmer’s quote is about effort over ability. Talent helps, but it is not the final word. Consistent hard work, hunger, and commitment can often take you further than raw skill alone.

stories.title: 'Bizarre thing...': Shashi Tharoor reacts to son Ishan being sacked by Washington Post
stories.summary: Reacting on X, Tharoor wrote: “The bizarre thing about this so-called ‘business decision’ by The Washington Post is that @ishaantharoor’s column flourished on the Internet,” adding that Ishaan Tharoor had “500,000 (half a million plus!) individual

stories.title: 'Pro-people, not rudderless': Mamata Banerjee hails Bengal budget; attacks Centre for denying funds to state
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP-led central government of withholding funds, yet her government presented a pro-people budget. The state's interim budget of Rs 4.06 lakh crore for 2026-27 includes increased allowances for women, youth, and frontline workers, notably boosting the Lakshmir Bhandar scheme by Rs 500 monthly.

stories.title: Meghalaya 'illegal' coal mine blast: 18 labourers dead; PM Modi expresses grief, announces ex-gratia
stories.summary: Tragedy struck Meghalaya's East Jaintia Hills as an explosion at a suspected illegal coal mine claimed at least 16 lives on Thursday. Several others remain trapped as rescue operations are underway. Officials confirmed the blast occurred in the Thangsku area, with one injured labourer hospitalized. The incident highlights the dangers of unscientific mining practices.

stories.title: 'Unprecedented': Lok Sabha passes Motion of Thanks on President's address without PM's speech; first since 2004
AspenKartier Animal Cruelty Arrest: Brookhaven police win PETA award; puppy rescued in Georgia
stories.summary: Brookhaven Police arrested Twitch streamer Aspen “AspenKartier” Easterling after viral clips allegedly captured her hitting her three month old puppy during a livestream. The dog was rescued and placed with DeKalb County Animal Services. Following the arrest on animal cruelty charges, PETA announced it will honor the department with a Compassionate Police Department Award for its swift action.

stories.title: Scientists believe early Earth was not green, it may have been purple: Know how scientists believe it's possible
Job scams in Saudi Arabia or UAE's Dubai, Abu Dhabi: How to spot fake offers, agents and avoid getting duped in the Gulf
stories.summary: Gulf job seekers face sophisticated scams, with fraudsters using AI and social media to lure victims. Authorities warn against upfront fees for visas or processing, unverified emails, and unrealistic offers. Always verify job offers through official government channels like MoHRE and MHRSD to avoid falling prey to these deceptive schemes.

stories.title: 'Bharat Taxi' will be rolled out across India in 3 years: Amit Shah at launch of co-op ride-hailing platform
stories.summary: Union cooperation minister Amit Shah launched 'Bharat Taxi', India's first cooperative-led ride-hailing platform, after a successful pilot. Initially available in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat, the service aims for nationwide expansion within three years, sharing profits directly with drivers. This indigenous platform offers zero-commission, surge-free pricing and social security benefits for its drivers.

stories.title: 'PM hiding behind Speaker': Opposition's sharp retort to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's remark on Modi speech, Congress 'plot'
Quote of the day by Albert Einstein: "The most beautiful experience we can have is..."
stories.summary: Albert Einstein’s quote celebrates curiosity and wonder. It reminds us that not knowing everything is not a weakness. It is the starting point of creativity, discovery, and real understanding.

stories.title: 'Requested PM not to come to House': Lok Sabha Speaker says plot by Congress MPs to create 'inappropriate incident'
stories.summary: Lok Sabha was adjourned amid security concerns over alleged Congress plans to attack Prime Minister Narendra Modi, despite his presence. Opposition rejected the claims, accusing the government of stalling proceedings. The Prime Minister is expected to address the Rajya Sabha later.

stories.title: Indian teacher Rouble Nagi, who painted educational murals across slums, wins Global Teacher Prize
stories.summary: Indian teacher and activist Rouble Nagi has won the Global Teacher Prize in Dubai for her work establishing over 800 learning centers and creating educational murals in slum areas. Nagi plans to use the $1 million prize to build an institute offering free vocational training to students, continuing her mission to make education accessible.

stories.title: Epstein files fallout: Why UK PM Keir Starmer is under fire
stories.summary: The Jeffrey Epstein scandal is creating political pressure for UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer over his past appointment of Peter Mandelson, who is now under criminal investigation. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump faces no immediate threat despite his name appearing in Epstein files, highlighting differing political environments and institutional responses to the ongoing global fallout.

stories.title: 'No such visit took place': MEA rubbishes report claiming Doval–Rubio meet before India-US trade deal
stories.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs has firmly denied a Bloomberg report alleging National Security Adviser Ajit Doval met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding a trade deal. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the claims baseless, stating no such meeting occurred. This rebuttal follows recent announcements of a trade agreement between India and the US.

stories.title: 'Energy security supreme priority': MEA replies to Trump's claim on Russian, Venezuelan oil; says decisions guided by national interest
Kuwait issues new Ramadan donation rules: Cash banned, Mosque collection prohibited
stories.summary: Kuwait has introduced strict new rules for Ramadan 2026 charitable donations, prohibiting cash collections in mosques and public spaces. Fundraising is limited to approved electronic methods like K-Net, online transfers, and apps, with prior ministry approval needed for foreign donations. The ministry also added single Kuwaiti women aged 30 and above as a new beneficiary category.

stories.title: Northern lights set to glow over Alaska, Canada and Greenland this week as solar activity rises
"Extremely frightening": Arvind Kejriwal flags up 807 people, mostly women and children, gone missing in 15 days in Delhi
stories.summary: AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal on Wednesday raised concern over the safety and security of vulnerables after 807 people, mostly women and children, went missing in the first 15 days of the year 2026.

stories.title: 'Khujli' vs 'abodh balak' jibe: Kharge and Nadda face-off in Rajya Sabha as Parliament logjam drags on
SC directs WB government to pay DA to employees by March; BJP hails verdict
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered West Bengal to pay dearness allowance to its employees as per the 2008 pay rules, stating financial constraints are no excuse. While upholding the entitlement to DA under state rules, the court clarified it's not a fundamental right, unlike a previous High Court ruling.

stories.title: Check-in from anywhere in Dubai? City Terminal Project's airport-free travel plan sounds unreal
stories.summary: Dubai is revolutionising air travel with its City Terminal Project, allowing passengers to check in and drop off luggage at city locations before being transported directly to their departure gates. This ambitious initiative aims to slash airport congestion and significantly enhance passenger experience, building on Dubai's status as a global aviation hub.

stories.title: The DIY therapy: When mental health advice comes from artificial intelligence
stories.summary: Online symptom checkers and social media are leading many to self-diagnose mental health conditions, often bypassing professional help. This trend, fueled by accessible yet often inaccurate content, risks misdiagnosis, inappropriate self-treatment, and delayed care, especially in regions with limited mental healthcare access. Experts urge caution, emphasizing the complexity of clinical diagnosis.

stories.title: Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj party moves Supreme Court challenging Bihar elections, seeks fresh polls
stories.summary: Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party has petitioned the Supreme Court, challenging the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections and demanding fresh polls. The party alleges the Bihar government violated the Model Code of Conduct by transferring Rs 10,000 to women beneficiaries after election schedules were announced, seeking the Election Commission's intervention.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi’s Nutri-Mark initiative explained: What it is, how will it transform food labels and health choices in 2026
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi has launched "Nutri-Mark," a pioneering front-of-pack nutrition labelling system using A-E grades to guide consumers and encourage healthier food products. This initiative, now mandatory for key categories, aims to combat rising obesity by simplifying nutritional information and promoting informed choices. Manufacturers are already reformulating products to achieve higher grades, fostering a healthier food environment.

stories.title: No more queues: Kuwait launches online passport update service for expatriates
stories.summary: Kuwait's Ministry of Interior has launched a new digital service via the Sahel app for expatriates to update passport details. This initiative eliminates the need for in-person visits to service centers, streamlining administrative processes and enhancing digital government efficiency for residents.

stories.title: GCC Unified Visa 2026 explained: Launch date, eligibility, fee, validity of Schengen-style visa for Gulf
stories.summary: Travellers will soon experience easier journeys across Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman. A unified tourist visa is set to launch in 2026. This single permit will allow visitors to explore all six Gulf nations without applying for individual visas. The initiative aims to boost tourism and economic integration.

stories.title: Congress digs out 2005 clip of Manmohan Singh to counter government amid Parliament logjam
Abu Dhabi prince with $20 billion fortune placed car order so big it shut down a Mercedes factory
stories.summary: Sheikh Hamad bin Hamdan al Nahyan earned the nickname “Rainbow Sheikh” after commissioning Mercedes-Benz to build seven W126 S-Class saloons, each finished in a different colour and fully colour-matched inside. The order, widely reported to have disrupted factory production, set the tone for a collection defined by extreme customisation and scale rather than conventional luxury.

stories.title: Is egg freezing only for married women?
stories.summary: Egg freezing in India is increasingly seen as a fertility preservation choice for all women, not just the married. Experts emphasize it empowers women to plan their reproductive future independently, offering flexibility to pursue careers and education without biological clock pressure. This proactive step is gaining traction among unmarried women, promoting informed decisions beyond societal norms.

stories.title: UAE: Abu Dhabi launches ‘World’s Richest Seas’ initiative to increase fish density by 2030
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi has launched a new marine programme, 'Hamdan bin Zayed: The World’s Richest Seas,' aiming for one of the highest fish densities globally by 2030. This initiative combines regulatory oversight, habitat restoration including artificial reefs and mangrove planting, and technology-led monitoring to rebuild fish populations and enhance marine ecosystem sustainability.

stories.title: Elon Musk plans solar-powered data centers in orbit, says “space is called space for a reason”
Saudi Arabia puts women on frontlines? KSA Interior Ministry graduates 328 female security recruits
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Security Directorate celebrated a significant milestone with 328 women graduating from basic security training. This marks a crucial step in integrating females into frontline roles, aligning with Vision 2030's reform agenda. The recruits are now equipped for diverse security assignments, enhancing the nation's operational capacity and promoting gender inclusion in national service.

stories.title: Passenger train derails in Odisha: New Jalpaiguri-Chennai Central SF goes off track near Jakhapura
stories.summary: The New Jalpaiguri–Chennai Central Superfast Express derailed near Jakhapura station in Odisha's Jajpur district at 8:51 am. One AC coach and two general coaches jumped off the tracks. No injuries or fatalities were reported, and passengers have been accommodated while the cause is investigated.

stories.title: 'None of their equipment worked’: Trump talks about US' ‘discombobulator’ use in Venezuela
Saudi Arabia launches camel passport: Digital system to track ownership and trade
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has launched a new digital Camel Passport initiative to bring order and traceability to its camel sector. This system creates official identities for registered camels, linking ownership, health records, and breed information to enhance regulation, veterinary services, and market confidence.

stories.title: UK aviation regulator seeks explanation from Air India over the Boeing fuel switch issue
stories.summary: The UK's aviation regulator has requested information from Air India regarding maintenance on a Boeing 787 after a fuel control switch issue was reported in London. While Air India conducted precautionary checks and found no further issues, an NGO has lodged a complaint, urging the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau to secure evidence and maintain its independence.

stories.title: THIS is the world’s deepest gold mine where workers travel 2.5 miles underground just to reach their jobs
Ramadan 2026 working hours in the UAE explained: Penalties and rules for private sector and government employees
stories.summary: UAE residents and workers are excited for Ramadan 2026, with mandatory reduced working hours for private and government sectors. Employees can expect at least two fewer hours daily in private firms, while government offices will operate from 9 am to 2:30 pm on weekdays. These adjustments aim to balance work with fasting and spiritual observance.

stories.title: The Washington post fires around 300 employees, scales back global reporting
stories.summary: The Washington Post has undergone significant layoffs, impacting a substantial portion of its workforce, including foreign affairs columnist Ishaan Tharoor and numerous international correspondents. This restructuring drastically curtails the newspaper's global coverage, leading to the closure of bureaus and the elimination of key sections. The move has drawn sharp criticism from former editors and staff.

stories.title: M R K Panneerselvam sparks row with ‘North Indians clean tables’ in Tamil Nadu remark; BJP hits back
stories.summary: The BJP has strongly criticised a Tamil Nadu minister's remarks about North Indian migrant workers, calling them derogatory and part of a pattern by the ruling DMK to fuel social divisions. The party highlighted the minister's comments about migrants working in low-paying jobs and questioned the silence of opposition alliance leaders, deeming such statements dangerous amidst rising violence against workers.

stories.title: Breast, cervical cancers rising steadily; deaths also climbing, govt data shows
Should Iran's supreme leader Khamenei be worried? Donald Trump's response and a blunt warning
stories.summary: President Trump issued a stern warning to Iran against restarting its nuclear program, threatening severe consequences if new facilities are established. He claimed US strikes had previously destroyed targeted nuclear sites, preventing Iran from accessing them and asserting that the country was close to developing a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: Savannah Guthrie says family is 'ready to talk' to person holding her mother: 'We need to know that she is alive'
Zealandia: Earth’s hidden continent beneath the Pacific
‘Can use a softer touch on immigration’: Trump says after Minneapolis shootings that killed 2
PM Modi to visit Malaysia on Feb 7-8
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Malaysia from February 7-8 to strengthen bilateral ties in trade, investment, energy, and maritime security. This visit, his third to Malaysia, follows the elevation of their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Modi will hold discussions with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and engage with the Indian diaspora and business leaders.

stories.title: ECI to hold meet of all state poll chiefs on February 24
Interview | ‘New I-T Act will help bring more clarity to processes, trigger higher compliance’: CBDT chairman
Pawar visits Sunetra at home, reignites reunification buzz
stories.summary: Amid reports of a division in the family, Pawar, Sunetra, her sons Parth and Jay, and other relatives held a closed-door meeting in their hometown late Wednesday, reigniting the reunification buzz. Pawar Senior and his wife Pratibha offered condolences to Ajit Pawar’s family, and together, they all met locals who visited them.

stories.title: Where’s your respected dad: SC to Choksi Junior
SC notice to govt on relaxation of NEET cut-off
Expect CJs of HCs to ensure speedy disposal of bail petitions: SC
stories.summary: After learning that issues relating to bail and pleas for suspension of sentence after conviction were pending in HCs for months and getting routinely adjourned, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi said, “We are extremely disappointed over the manner in which matters relating to personal liberty of individuals are dealt with by the HCs.”

stories.title: HR exec caught in Coldplay kiss cam scandal set to host $875 crisis conference
Danish war veteran who lost both legs says he feels 'betrayed' by Trump’s Nato remarks
Nishikant takes a page out of Rahul’s book to attack Congress
stories.summary: Dubey’s move was seen as BJP’s bid to turn the heat on Congress, which has been attacking Modi over bits of the unpublished book authored by ex-Army chief Gen M M Naravane (retd), and it further riled up the protesting opposition MPs in LS, who turned up the noise and tore papers, but not before the fourth-term member had his say for over a couple of minutes.

stories.title: Branded ‘traitor’ by Rahul, Beant’s grandson hits back, calls Gandhi scion ‘desh ke dushman’
stories.summary: The exchange — which took place at the main entrance of the Parliament building, where Rahul was standing in solidarity with the eight MPs who are on protest since being suspended from the Lok Sabha a day earlier — was caught on video and promptly went viral. It was also circulated by Congress.

stories.title: Bengal SIR row: Will rectify errors of ‘logical discrepancy,’ says SC
stories.summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi said voters’ names should not be struck off the electoral rolls because of errors creeping into spelling of names during translation from Bengali to English or vice-versa. “We will ensure that it is rectified,” the bench said.

stories.title: Manipur gets Meitei CM with Kuki, Naga as deputies
stories.summary: Governor AK Bhalla also administered the oath of office to BJP's Konthoujam Govindas and Khuraijam Loken Singh of NPP as cabinet ministers at the Lok Bhavan ceremony, which ended almost a year of President’s rule since N Biren Singh resigned over criticism of the previous govt's handling of the violence that erupted in May 2023.

stories.title: 'Baffled': US woman faces charges for rescuing abandoned dog from freezing snowstorm
At 93, Apollo founder still has big dreams for Indian healthcare
stories.summary: Dr Reddy, who turns 93 Thursday, lobbied PM Indira Gandhi to ensure import duties on equipment fell from 300% to zero. Banks funded the build; cement and steel came cheap, and he built Apollo Chennai, India’s first multispecialty hospital, in 1983 with a promise to offer treatment to 25% of patients free.

stories.title: India crude buy helps global market stability: Russia
ED achieved 95% conviction rate in PMLA cases: Govt
stories.summary: “As on Dec 31, 2025, the special PMLA courts have delivered judgments, on merits, on the issue of money laundering in 58 cases, out of which conviction orders have been passed in 55 cases, convicting 123 accused,” MoS for finance Pankaj Chaudhary told Rajya Sabha in a written response to a question.

stories.title: SC flags undervaluation, sham auctions under IBC, seeks probe
stories.summary: Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Anil Ambani group, said such a sale was a public process, whether the buyer was a brother or anyone else. But the CJI-led bench said, “Unfortunately, IBC proceedings are misused nowadays. The assets of a company in debt are undervalued. Then it is put on a sham auction and, in a planned manner, a family member or a friend buys it.”

stories.title: India, 6-nation Gulf bloc to kick off FTA talks
Supreme Court asks Centre to review Wangchuk’s detention
stories.summary: SC had earlier directed authorities to conduct Wangchuk’s medical examination by a specialised doctor and file a report before it. The activist is currently lodged in Jodhpur jail. The medical report was placed before the apex court during the last hearing. Wangchuk was detained on Sept 26 last year under the National Security Act following protests in Leh over demands of statehood and Sixth Schedule status for Ladakh.

stories.title: Regulator orders probe into IndiGo’s ‘unfair business practices’
stories.summary: Bengaluru-based Kartikeya Rawal had moved CCI after his flight on Dec 5 last year was cancelled and alternative ones were available only at higher prices. He alleged the overcharging by IndiGo was “abuse of dominance”. The airline contested the claim, while arguing that CCI did not have jurisdiction in the case.

stories.title: Prevent systematic pattern of violence, threats against our WB staff: EC to SC
stories.summary: Comparing smooth conduct of SIR in other states to that in Bengal where those involved in the roll revision have been “targeted”, EC, in its affidavit, said, “It unequivocally illustrates that the challenges encountered in West Bengal are not intrinsic to the SIR process itself, but are a direct result of the inadequacies of the state machinery and the prevailing climate of political interference therein.”

stories.title: PM’s reply deferred as protest stalls Lok Sabha; scared Modi ran away, says opposition
stories.summary: The adjournment was a fallout of the stand-off between the two sides over Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s insistence on citing the unpublished book of former Army chief, Gen M M Naravane. The confrontation intensified due to what was seen as a tit-for-tat response by BJP member Nishikant Dubey, who sought to quote from books replete with unflattering references to members of the Gandhi-Nehru clan.

stories.title: ‘Allow me, sir’: Mamata argues against SIR in Supreme Court
stories.summary: West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, a law graduate and perhaps the first CM to argue in-person before the apex court, watched for 20 minutes, as SC heard West Bengal counsel Shyam Divan on irregularities in SIR in the state. She was heard telling TMC’s Kalyan Banerjee “bolbo toh aaji (I will speak today)”.
